title: # [Bug/Crash] Second `design()` call on the same object crashes in LTB buckling check (`math domain error`)
body:
**Environment**
- OsdagBridge `dev` @ `d74f56d` (2026-07-26)
- macOS (Intel), conda env `osdagbridge-env`, Python 3.12.16
- Headless: `PlateGirderBridge().set_input(d); design(); design()` on the SAME object (proper `__main__` guard; no harness re-exec)
- Finding type: **T1 (confirmed crash — executed)**

**Scenario — what we filled (exact inputs)**
Default bridge built from `BASIC_INPUT_DICT` + `solve_extend_basic_input_dict` + material priming, no fields invented: span 30.0 m, carriageway 10.5 m, skew 0°, footpath None, median No, design mode Optimized, default materials (E 350A, M40). Layout solver gives 7 girders @ 2.28 m, D = 1.67 m. This is the normal case that completes fine on its own (SW01/SMOKE, ~70–130 s).

**What we got (executed, `dictionaries/IDEM2/same.log`, `evidence/logs/determinism_2.log`)**
- `design()` call #1 → **RUN1_DONE**, completes normally (max_DCR 1.871, as in the standalone case).
- `design()` call #2 on the same object → **crash**:
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../same.py", line 11, in <module>
    b.design(); o2=...
  File ".../plategirderbridge.py", line 757, in design
    self.run_stage("5", self.run_dcr_checks, dataset)
  File ".../designer.py", line 1802, in compute_all
    ltb = self.compute_buckling_resistance(...)
  File ".../designer.py", line 1007, in compute_buckling_resistance
    res = IRC22_2014.cl603_3_3_1_buckling_resistance_moment(...)
  File ".../irc22_2015.py", line 639, in cl603_3_3_1_buckling_resistance_moment
    lambda_LT = math.sqrt(beta_b * (Zp * fy) / Mcr)
ValueError: math domain error
Stage 5 (DCR checks) → LTB buckling resistance. Exit code 1.

**Expected vs actual (the mistake)**
- **Expected:** calling `design()` twice on the same object (as happens when a user unlocks inputs and clicks Design again in the same session) should either produce consistent results or be explicitly reset — it should not crash.
- **Actual:** the second call crashes with `math domain error`, i.e. the argument to `sqrt` in the LTB check went negative/zero on the second run. Some state from run 1 is not reset before run 2 (the design() start calls `self.memory.release()` but section/DTO state appears to persist).

**Root cause (file:line, read-only)**
`src/osdagbridge/core/utils/codes/irc22_2015.py:639`:
```py
term1 = (math.pi ** 2 * E * Iy) / (LLT ** 2)
term2 = (G * It) + (math.pi ** 2 * E * Iw) / (LLT ** 2)
Mcr = math.sqrt(term1 * term2)  # Nmm
lambda_LT = math.sqrt(beta_b * (Zp * fy) / Mcr)   # <-- L639 ValueError on 2nd run
Called from designer.py:1007 (compute_buckling_resistance). On the second run one of Zp, fy, Mcr or beta_b takes a value that makes the radicand negative/zero — consistent with stale girder-section state carried over from run 1. Exact stale field under investigation.
Logs and proof
- scripts/determinism_check.py (with __main__ guard), dictionaries/IDEM2/same.py, dictionaries/IDEM2/same.log
- evidence/logs/determinism_2.log (RUN1_DONE then ValueError), full traceback in dictionaries/IDEM2/same.log tail
- Note: an earlier unguarded harness (dictionaries/IDEM/same.log) showed a forkserver re-exec artifact; it was discarded. The report relies only on the guarded IDEM2 run.
Suggested fix (diff idea)
- Reset all per-run section/DTO/check state at the start of design() (not just OpenSees memory), or guard the LTB computation:
  # irc22_2015.py, before the sqrt
+ if Mcr <= 0 or (beta_b * Zp * fy) <= 0:
+     raise ValueError(f"Invalid LTB input on design run: Mcr={Mcr}, Zp={Zp}, fy={fy} — reset design state before reuse.")
  lambda_LT = math.sqrt(beta_b * (Zp * fy) / Mcr)
- Add an idempotence regression test: two consecutive design() calls on one object must not crash and must give equal outputs.
Duplicate check
Searched refreshed issues (open+closed, 131 items) via scripts/search_issues.py for second run, math domain, Mcr, buckling resistance, redesign: #85 (3D CAD not displayed after unlock/redesign) is the closest "second run in same session" issue but concerns CAD display and reports no design-error dialog; this is a hard crash in the 2nd design() at stage 5. No duplicate found.
Notes
Reported as T1 (confirmed crash) — executed with a guarded harness, reproducible, exact traceback. Related to the "reuse backend object" state area (#85, #125) but a distinct failure mode.

title: # [Bug/Analysis] Valid input silently skips live load → all design demands = 0 and verdict PASS (wrong PASS)
body:
**Environment**
- OsdagBridge `dev` @ `d74f56d` (2026-07-26)
- macOS (Intel), conda env `osdagbridge-env`, Python 3.12.16
- Headless design via `PlateGirderBridge().set_input(d); design()` from `BASIC_INPUT_DICT` + `solve_extend_basic_input_dict` + material priming (no GUI, no baseline.osi)
- Finding type: **T1 (confirmed wrong PASS — executed and reproduced)**

**Scenario — what we filled (exact inputs, case SW05 / repro P5_SW05R)**
All values from the app's own default flow; only these changed:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| structure.type | Highway Bridge |
| geometry.span | 30.0 m |
| geometry.carriageway_width | **7.5 m** (minimum allowed with median) |
| geometry.skew_angle | 0.0° |
| geometry.footpath | **Both Sides** |
| geometry.include_median | **Yes** |
| geometry.design_mode | Optimized |
| materials | defaults (E 350A, M40) |

All inputs are within documented limits (median allowed only with cw ≥ 7.5 m — satisfied). The bridge is geometrically valid.

**What we got (executed output, `dictionaries/P5_SW05R/output.json`, `dictionaries/SW05/output.json`)**
- Root warning in log: `analyser.py:1998 UserWarning: Envelope-based governing LL detection failed ("not all values found in index 'Element'. Try setting the method keyword argument (example: method='nearest')."); skipping LL creation.` followed by 26× `'live_load'/'thermal_load' load case not available` warnings.
- Design check table:
  - `ULS Flexure  0.00 / 11498.55 → 0.000 PASS`
  - `ULS Shear  0.00 → 0.000 PASS`, `M-V Interaction 0.000 PASS`
  - `steeldesign.details.moment.mu_applied = 0.0` (compare normal cases ≈ 2600 kN·m)
  - all `util.* = 0.0`
- **OVERALL VERDICT: Status PASS, Maximum DCR 0.2853** (the only nonzero/failing check is a stiffener check `Int.Stiff: Leg ≤ H_limit = 1.479 FAIL`, which is excluded from the structural DCR set — so the design is reported as PASS).

**Controls (same build method, only one field changed — all show 0 warnings and normal demands)**
- `P5_MED_NOFOOT` (median Yes, footpath None): `mu_applied = 2943.66`, flexure 25.4%, fatigue 206.8% — 0 live-load warnings.
- `P5_FOOT_NOMED` (footpath Both Sides, median No): `mu_applied = 2652.52`, flexure 22.9%, fatigue 186.3% — 0 warnings.
- `P5_MED_CW105` (median Yes + Both Sides, cw 10.5 m): `mu_applied = 3442.47`, flexure 29.75%, fatigue 242.35% — 0 warnings.
So the trigger is specifically the **combination of median Yes + Both Sides footpath + cw exactly 7.5 m + zero skew**; each near-neighbor works.

**Expected vs actual (the mistake)**
- **Expected:** a valid bridge with live load present must have nonzero flexure/shear demand and a realistic utilisation; if live-load detection genuinely fails, the design should abort with a clear error, not report PASS.
- **Actual:** live-load case creation silently fails (a caught xarray `.sel` lookup error), the ULS envelope is built with zero vehicle load, all structural demands become 0, and the design is reported **PASS** — a dangerously unconservative result for a bridge design tool.

**Logs and proof**
- `scripts/design_runner.py`, `scripts/oracle_runs.py`, `test_cases/built/SW05.params.json`, `test_cases/built/P5_SW05R.input.json`
- `dictionaries/SW05/case.log` (root warning + 26 live-load warnings), `dictionaries/P5_SW05R/run.log`
- `dictionaries/P5_SW05R/output.json` (mu=0.0, all utils 0.0), controls `dictionaries/P5_MED_NOFOOT/output.json`, `dictionaries/P5_FOOT_NOMED/output.json`, `dictionaries/P5_MED_CW105/output.json`
- `evidence/logs/design_sweep_run.log` (SW05 ok, 132.8 s)

**Root cause (file:line, read-only)**
`src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/analyser.py:1988-2003` in `create_governing_ll_load_case()`:
```py
gov_element = env_val.idxmax("Element").item()
governing_lc = str(env_lc.sel(Element=gov_element).values)   # L1991 KeyError when the governing
                                                             # element id is absent from env_lc's
                                                             # 'Element' index (median/footpath layout)
...
except Exception as exc:
    warnings.warn(f"Envelope-based governing LL detection failed ({exc}); skipping LL creation.")
    self.ll_load_case = None        # L1998: LL case never created
    return dataset
Then create_dl_ll_combination() (≈L2100) warns live-load case not available and builds a combo with no LL; with no ULS load case, the design envelope reports zero flexural/shear demand. The broad except Exception swallows the lookup error and continues to PASS.
Suggested fix (diff idea)
-            governing_lc = str(env_lc.sel(Element=gov_element).values)
+            governing_lc = str(env_lc.sel(Element=gov_element, method="nearest").values)
@@
-        except Exception as exc:
-            warnings.warn(f"Envelope-based governing LL detection failed ({exc}); skipping LL creation.")
-            self.ll_load_case = None
-            return dataset
+        except Exception as exc:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "Governing live-load detection failed; refusing to produce a design with zero live load."
+            ) from exc
At minimum, do not silently continue to a PASS verdict when the governing LL case cannot be determined — fail loudly.
Duplicate check
Searched refreshed issues (open+closed, 131 items) via scripts/search_issues.py: #87 (seismic uses zero LL mass because it runs before governing-vehicle selection) and #45 (missing DCR categories written as 0.0 on output dock) are related but have different triggers; #92 is thermal load cases. No duplicate found for "governing LL detection fails → all ULS demand zero → PASS".
Notes
Reported as T1 (confirmed) because the wrong PASS is executed and reproduced (SW05 and P5_SW05R) with the exact input isolated and near-neighbor controls showing nonzero demands.

title: # [Bug/Performance] Valid inputs (span 45 m + median + footpaths) make `design()` run >10 minutes without completing
body:
**Environment**
- OsdagBridge `dev` @ `d74f56d` (2026-07-26)
- macOS (Intel), conda env `osdagbridge-env`, Python 3.12.16
- Headless design via `PlateGirderBridge().set_input(d); design()` from `BASIC_INPUT_DICT` + `solve_extend_basic_input_dict` + material priming (no GUI, no baseline.osi)
- Finding type: **T2 (likely performance/hang bug)**

**Scenario — what we filled (exact inputs)**
All inputs from the app's own default flow; only these were changed:

| Field | SW03 value | SW06 value |
|---|---|---|
| geometry.span | 45.0 m | 45.0 m |
| geometry.carriageway_width | 15.0 m | 15.0 m |
| geometry.skew_angle | −15.0° | +15.0° |
| geometry.footpath | Both Sides | Single Side |
| geometry.include_median | Yes | Yes |
| geometry.design_mode | Optimized | Optimized |
| materials | defaults (E 350A, M40) | defaults |

All values are within the documented limits (span ≤45, cw ≤23.6, skew ±15, median only with cw≥7.5). The bridge is geometrically valid.

**What we got (executed)**
- SW03: `design()` did **not** finish within the 600 s (10-min) per-case timeout — killed at 600.2 s (`evidence/logs/design_sweep_run.log`, `dictionaries/SW03/case.log`, `dictionaries/SW03/result.json` absent). A second run with no timeout consumed **>12 min CPU** and still produced no result before being stopped (`evidence/logs/SW03_rerun.log`).
- SW06 (same span/cw/median, skew +15, footpath Single Side): also timed out at 600.1 s.
- The SW03 case log stalls after repeated `UserWarning: ... 'thermal_load' load case not available` and shows earlier `RuntimeWarning: The iteration is not making good progress ... fsolve` from `ospgrillage/utils.py:555`, i.e. the run is stuck in the analysis/envelope stage, not producing output.
- **Controls that complete normally** (same harness): span 30/cw 10.5/no median/no footpath = 71–79 s; span 45/cw 10.5/no median/no footpath (`OR_SPAN45`) = 77.5 s; span 30/cw 15 = 100 s; span 30 + footpath Both Sides = 121 s. So the slow/hanging cases are specifically the combination of **max span (45 m) + median + footpaths**.

**Expected vs actual (the mistake)**
- **Expected:** a valid input within documented limits should complete in a time comparable to other valid cases (tens of seconds to a couple of minutes), or raise a clear error.
- **Actual:** `design()` runs indefinitely (>10 min, no result) for these valid inputs, so a user pressing Design would see the app hang with no result.

**Logs and proof**
- `scripts/design_sweep.py`, `scripts/design_runner.py`, `test_cases/built/SW03.params.json`, `SW06.params.json`
- `evidence/logs/design_sweep_run.log` (SW03/SW06 timeout lines), `evidence/logs/SW03_rerun.log`, `dictionaries/SW03/case.log`, `dictionaries/SW06/case.log`
- Controls: `dictionaries/SMOKE/result.json`, `dictionaries/OR_SPAN45/result.json`, `evidence/logs/oracle_runs3.log`

**Likely area (root cause not pinned)**
Analysis/moving-load envelope stage: `ospgrillage/utils.py:555` `fsolve` non-convergence on the oblique grillage with many components (median + both footpaths) at the maximum span; the repeated `'thermal_load' load case not available` warnings indicate stage 4F/4G. Exact line under investigation.

**Suggested fix (direction)**
- Bound the moving-load/envelope solver (iteration cap / tolerance) so non-convergent cases terminate with a clear warning instead of hanging.
- Investigate why median + footpaths at max span prevents convergence; add a regression test with this input that must complete within a time budget.

**Duplicate check**
Searched open+closed issues (refreshed `notes/issues_raw.json`, 131 items) via `scripts/search_issues.py` for `hang`, `slow`, `timeout`, `non-converg` — no matching issue about `design()` hanging on valid span-45 + median/footpath inputs. **No duplicate found.**

**Notes**
Reported as T2 (likely): reproduced twice (SW03 twice, SW06 once) and controls complete quickly; but it is a performance/non-termination issue rather than a wrong numeric result.

title: # [Bug/Analysis] Skew sign is not mirror-symmetric: +15° and −15° give different design demands for a symmetric bridge
body:
**Environment**
- OsdagBridge `dev` @ `d74f56d` (2026-07-26)
- macOS (Intel), conda env `osdagbridge-env`, Python 3.12.16
- Headless design via `PlateGirderBridge().set_input(d); design()` from `BASIC_INPUT_DICT` + `solve_extend_basic_input_dict` (no GUI, no baseline.osi)
- Finding type: **T2 (likely analysis bug — sign-dependent results)**

**Scenario — what we filled (exact inputs)**
Two runs, identical in every field except the sign of the skew angle:

| Field | Value (both runs) |
|---|---|
| structure.type | Highway Bridge |
| geometry.span | 30.0 m |
| geometry.carriageway_width | 10.5 m |
| geometry.include_median | No |
| geometry.footpath | None |
| geometry.design_mode | Optimized |
| materials | defaults (E 350A girder/CB/ED, M40 deck) |
| geometry.skew_angle | **+15.0°** (run A) / **−15.0°** (run B) |

All remaining inputs came from the app's own default flow (`BASIC_INPUT_DICT` → `solve_extend_basic_input_dict` → material priming); no value was invented. The bridge cross-section is symmetric (no median, no footpath), so +15° and −15° are mirror images of each other.

A second, independent pair used the same inputs with skew **+7.5°** vs **−7.5°**.

**What we got (executed output, `dictionaries/OR_SKEW15`, `OR_SKEWM15`, `OR_SKEW75`, `OR_SKEWM75`)**

| Quantity | +15° | −15° | +7.5° | −7.5° |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `steeldesign.details.moment.mu_applied` (kNm) | 2602.12 | 2376.38 | 2582.22 | 2488.43 |
| `util.shear` (%) | 59.28 | 41.08 | 62.32 | 42.18 |
| `util.fatigue` (%) | 183.74 | 167.06 | 182.25 | 175.33 |
| `util.flexure` (%) | 22.67 | 20.71 | 22.50 | 21.68 |
| `util.deflection_crack` (%) | 55.06 | 49.13 | — | — |

For reference, quantities that depend only on self-weight are **identical** across signs: `util.long_trans_shear = 21.52` in both ±15° runs; `Int.Stiff: Leg ≤ H_limit = 1.479` in both. So the geometry/section itself is mirrored correctly — the divergence appears in load-driven checks (shear, fatigue, deflection, flexure).

**Expected vs actual (the mistake)**
- **Expected:** for a symmetric cross-section, flipping the skew sign mirrors the structure. Every demand/utilisation magnitude should be the same (the controlling girder moves from one edge to the other, but the maximum over all girders is unchanged). A ±15° pair should differ by ~0%, not by 9–44%.
- **Actual:** the positive-skew runs are consistently and substantially higher — `util.shear` is **59.3 vs 41.1** (+15°) and **62.3 vs 42.2** (+7.5°), i.e. ~44–48% higher; design moment differs by ~9%. This means the analysis result depends on the *sign* of a symmetric geometric parameter, which is not physical.

**Why this matters:** a user entering +15° instead of −15° (same physical bridge, mirrored) gets a materially different design — different governing shear/fatigue utilisations and potentially a different PASS/FAIL verdict. It indicates the load application or grillage response is not mirrored with the geometry.

**Logs and proof**
- `scripts/oracle_runs.py` (cases `OR_SKEW15`, `OR_SKEWM15`, `OR_SKEW75`, `OR_SKEWM75`), `scripts/design_runner.py`
- `dictionaries/OR_SKEW15/output.json`, `dictionaries/OR_SKEWM15/output.json`, `dictionaries/OR_SKEW75/output.json`, `dictionaries/OR_SKEWM75/output.json`
- DCR tables parsed from `dictionaries/OR_SKEW15/case.log` etc.; `evidence/logs/oracle_runs1.log`, `evidence/logs/oracle_runs2.log`

**Likely area (root cause not yet pinned to a line)**
`src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/analyser.py` builds the grillage with `create_grillage(..., skew=self.angle, mesh_type="Oblique")` (≈L275) and applies loads through `LoadPlacementManager` (`load_placement.py`: deck/footpath/median line & patch loads defined in local x–z coordinates). If moving-vehicle placement or the oblique mesh is not mirrored when the skew sign flips, the positive sign will systematically attract more load. This is the area to inspect; the exact line is still being traced.

**Suggested fix (direction)**
Ensure live-load placement and oblique-mesh node/load mapping are mirror-invariant: when `skew → −skew`, the set of applied vehicle/patch loads and their distribution among girders should be the mirror image, giving identical maximum demands. Add a regression test asserting that DCR magnitudes for +θ and −θ match within tolerance for a symmetric section.

**Duplicate check**
Searched open+closed issues (full titles/bodies, refreshed `notes/issues_raw.json`, 131 items) via `scripts/search_issues.py` for `skew`, `mirror`, `asymmetric` — closest are #89 (skewed bridges retain only one per-girder result) and #124 (inconsistent overall width), neither of which compares +θ vs −θ sign. **No duplicate found.**

**Notes**
Reported as T2 (likely) because the expectation is well-justified by symmetry but the exact responsible line is still under investigation. Confirmed reproducible in two independent sign pairs.

title: # [Bug/I-O] `saveOSI_inputs` uses `yaml.dump` (unsafe tags) while load uses `yaml.safe_load` — round-trip can fail
body:
**Environment**
- OsdagBridge `dev` @ `d74f56d` (2026-07-26)
- macOS (Intel), conda env `osdagbridge-env`, Python 3.12.16
- Finding type: **T2 (likely save/load round-trip bug)**

**Description**
`TemplatePage.saveOSI_inputs` writes the input dictionary with `yaml.dump(...)` (default/unsafe dumper), while `loadOSI_inputs` reads with `yaml.safe_load(...)`. For certain Python/object types that can appear in state (e.g. numpy scalars, tuples, sets), `yaml.dump` emits Python-specific tags (`!!python/...`, `!!set`, `!!python/tuple`) that `yaml.safe_load` refuses to construct, causing a saved OSI file to fail loading.

**Steps / Reproduction (executed, direct YAML behavior)**
```python
import yaml, numpy as np
d = {"a": np.float64(1.5), "t": (1, 2), "s": {1, 2}, "f": 1.5}
dumped = yaml.dump(d)
print(dumped)
yaml.safe_load(dumped)  # raises ConstructorError
Observed (executed)
- Dump includes !!python/object/apply:numpy._core.multiarray.scalar, !!set, !!python/tuple
- yaml.safe_load(dumped) raises:
ConstructorError: could not determine a constructor for the tag 'tag:yaml.org,2002:python/object/apply:numpy._core.multiarray.scalar'
(Evidence: evidence/logs/trackI_yaml_dump_safe_load.txt)
Code (read-only, file:line)
- Save: src/osdagbridge/desktop/ui/template_page.py (~793–820) — yaml.dump(self.input_dict, input_file) then shows "Saved OSI Successfully!"
- Load: src/osdagbridge/desktop/ui/template_page.py (~827–850+) — data = yaml.safe_load(f) then validates/populates
Expected behavior
OSI save and load should be round-trip compatible: files saved by the app should be loadable by the app without unsafe/Python-specific tags that safe_load cannot parse.
Actual behavior
Save uses unsafe yaml.dump while load enforces yaml.safe_load, so dictionaries containing types like numpy scalars/tuples/sets can be written but not read back.
Impact
Potential data-loss/UX issue: a user can save successfully but fail to reload the same OSI if such types are present in self.input_dict.
Suggested fix (diff idea)
Serialize with a safe, JSON-like representation (or normalize types before dumping) and/or use yaml.safe_dump with explicit representers for supported types:
-            with open(filePath, 'w') as input_file:
-                yaml.dump(self.input_dict, input_file)
+            with open(filePath, 'w') as input_file:
+                yaml.safe_dump(self.input_dict, input_file, sort_keys=False)
Additionally, normalize values before save (e.g. convert numpy scalars to Python float/int, tuples to lists, sets to sorted lists) to preserve compatibility.
Duplicate check
Searched refreshed issues (open+closed, through #129 context / refreshed this session) via scripts/search_issues.py for yaml.dump, python/object, safe_load usage patterns — no matching issue found for unsafe-dump vs safe-load round-trip failure. (Not #96/#67/#69; #99 mentions yaml.dump/safe_load only as dependency usage context.)
Logs / proof
- evidence/logs/trackI_yaml_dump_safe_load.txt

title: # [Bug/Validation] Integer validators raise `OverflowError` on `inf`/`-inf` instead of returning a validation message
body:
**Environment**
- OsdagBridge `dev` @ `d74f56d` (2026-07-26)
- macOS (Intel), conda env `osdagbridge-env`, Python 3.12.16
- Executed via direct validator calls (no GUI, no design run)
- Finding type: **T2 (likely bug — exception instead of handled validation error)**

**Description**
For several integer-valued additional-input keys, `BridgeInputValidator.validate_additional_inputs` raises `OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer` when given `float('inf')` or `float('-inf')`, instead of returning a corrected value/message like other invalid inputs.

**Steps / Reproduction (executed)**
```python
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "OsdagBridge/src")
from osdagbridge.core.bridge_types.plate_girder.validator import BridgeInputValidator
from osdagbridge.core.utils import common as C

bv = BridgeInputValidator()
for key in [
    C.KEY_TS_NO_OF_GIRDERS,
    C.KEY_WC_LD_LANE_TABLE_COUNT,
    C.KEY_MP_CB_NO_OF_CROSS_BRACINGS,
    C.KEY_DS_STUD_COUNT,
    C.KEY_DO_LOAD_CYCLES,
]:
    for v in (float("inf"), float("-inf")):
        try:
            print(key, v, bv.validate_additional_inputs(key, {key: v}))
        except Exception as e:
            print(key, v, type(e).__name__, e)
Observed (executed)
- typical_section.no_of_girders inf/-inf → OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer
- typical_section.lane_details.lane_table_count inf/-inf → OverflowError
- member_properties.cross_bracing_details.no_of_cross_bracings inf/-inf → OverflowError
- design_options.shear_studs.count inf/-inf → OverflowError
- design_options_cont.fatigue.load_cycles inf/-inf → OverflowError
(10 exception cases total; scripts/validator_fuzz.py, evidence/logs/trackF_validator_fuzz.txt, evidence/logs/trackF_validator_fuzz.json)
Expected behavior
Non-finite or otherwise invalid numeric inputs should be handled gracefully and produce a validation correction/message (or a controlled error), not an uncaught exception.
Actual behavior
inf/-inf for these integer fields triggers OverflowError during int conversion inside validation.
Root cause (likely, file:line)
src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/validator.py — integer-field branches parse via _to_int (which does int(float(...))/similar) without guarding non-finite values before conversion, e.g. KEY_TS_NO_OF_GIRDERS branch around L191–199 uses self._to_int(...).
Suggested fix (diff idea)
Reject non-finite values before integer conversion (in _to_int and/or per-field checks):
 def _to_int(self, value):
-    try:
-        return int(float(value))
-    except Exception:
-        return None
+    try:
+        v = float(value)
+    except Exception:
+        return None
+    if not math.isfinite(v):
+        return None
+    return int(v)
(Ensure callers return an appropriate validation message when parsed value is None due to non-finite input.)
Duplicate check
Searched refreshed issues (open+closed, notes/issues_raw.json through #129 context / refreshed this session) via scripts/search_issues.py for OverflowError and infinity — no matching issue found. #88 covers NaN/nonfinite acceptance in different context; this is an uncaught exception on inf for specific integer validators.
Logs / proof
- scripts/validator_fuzz.py
- evidence/logs/trackF_validator_fuzz.txt
- evidence/logs/trackF_validator_fuzz.json

title: # [Bug/Validation] `validate_material_inputs` skips range checks for cross-bracing/end-diaphragm material keys
body:
**Environment**
- OsdagBridge `dev` @ `d74f56d` (2026-07-26)
- macOS (Intel), conda env `osdagbridge-env`, Python 3.12.16
- Executed via direct validator calls (no design run, no `baseline.osi`)
- Finding type: **T2 (likely validation bug/gap)**

**Description**
`BridgeInputValidator.validate_material_inputs` enforces per-field numeric ranges for girder and deck custom material properties, but it has no validation branches for cross-bracing or end-diaphragm material keys. As a result, out-of-range values for `material.cross_bracing.*` and `material.end_diaphragm.*` are accepted (function returns `None`) instead of being corrected/rejected like equivalent girder/deck fields.

**Steps / Reproduction (executed)**
From a Python session with `OsdagBridge/src` on `sys.path`:
```python
from osdagbridge.core.bridge_types.plate_girder.validator import BridgeInputValidator
from osdagbridge.core.utils.common import (
    KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_FY,
    KEY_MATERIAL_CROSS_BRACING_FY, KEY_MATERIAL_CROSS_BRACING_FU,
    KEY_MATERIAL_CROSS_BRACING_E, KEY_MATERIAL_CROSS_BRACING_DENSITY,
    KEY_MATERIAL_END_DIAPHRAGM_FY, KEY_MATERIAL_END_DIAPHRAGM_FU,
    KEY_MATERIAL_END_DIAPHRAGM_DENSITY,
)

bv = BridgeInputValidator()

# girder (range enforced)
print(bv.validate_material_inputs(KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_FY, {KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_FY: 5000}))
# -> (1200.0, 'Yield Strength, Fy must be between 100.0 and 1200.0 MPa.')

# cross-bracing / end-diaphragm (no branch -> accepted)
print(bv.validate_material_inputs(KEY_MATERIAL_CROSS_BRACING_FY, {KEY_MATERIAL_CROSS_BRACING_FY: 5000}))
print(bv.validate_material_inputs(KEY_MATERIAL_END_DIAPHRAGM_FY, {KEY_MATERIAL_END_DIAPHRAGM_FY: 5000}))
print(bv.validate_material_inputs(KEY_MATERIAL_CROSS_BRACING_FU, {KEY_MATERIAL_CROSS_BRACING_FU: 2000}))
print(bv.validate_material_inputs(KEY_MATERIAL_CROSS_BRACING_E, {KEY_MATERIAL_CROSS_BRACING_E: 500}))
print(bv.validate_material_inputs(KEY_MATERIAL_CROSS_BRACING_DENSITY, {KEY_MATERIAL_CROSS_BRACING_DENSITY: 200}))
print(bv.validate_material_inputs(KEY_MATERIAL_END_DIAPHRAGM_FU, {KEY_MATERIAL_END_DIAPHRAGM_FU: 2000}))
print(bv.validate_material_inputs(KEY_MATERIAL_END_DIAPHRAGM_DENSITY, {KEY_MATERIAL_END_DIAPHRAGM_DENSITY: 200}))
# -> None for each (accepted)
Expected behavior
Custom material per-field range validation should apply consistently to steel components that accept custom material properties (girder, cross bracing, end diaphragm), or the validator should clearly scope/handle unsupported component keys so out-of-range CB/ED values are not silently accepted.
Actual behavior
validate_material_inputs validates KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_* and KEY_MATERIAL_DECK_* only; material.cross_bracing.* and material.end_diaphragm.* keys (and no stiffener material keys are defined in common.py) fall through to return None, so out-of-range values are accepted.
Logs / proof
scripts/drift_check.py
evidence/logs/phase3_drift_check.txt (executed output showing girder rejected, CB/ED accepted for extreme values)
Root cause (file:line, read-only)
src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/validator.py — BridgeInputValidator.validate_material_inputs (≈L78–L172) contains conditional branches only for girder and deck material keys:
# ── Weight Density (kN/m³) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
if key == KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_DENSITY:
    ...
# ── Yield Strength, Fy (MPa) ────────────────────────────────────────────
elif key == KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_FY:
    ...
...
# ── Deck: ... ──
elif key == KEY_MATERIAL_DECK_THERMAL:
    ...
return None
No corresponding branches exist for KEY_MATERIAL_CROSS_BRACING_* or KEY_MATERIAL_END_DIAPHRAGM_* (defined in core/utils/common.py, e.g. L76–L90), so those keys are not range-checked.
Suggested fix (diff idea)
Add per-field validation for cross-bracing and end-diaphragm material keys using the same steel ranges as girder (or component-appropriate ranges if specified), e.g. by handling CB/ED Fy/Fu/E/G/Poisson/Thermal/Density alongside girder branches (or via shared helper). Example sketch:
diff --git a/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/validator.py b/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/validator.py
--- a/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/validator.py
+++ b/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/validator.py
@@
-        # ── Yield Strength, Fy (MPa) ────────────────────────────────────────────
-        elif key == KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_FY:
+        # ── Yield Strength, Fy (MPa) — steel members ────────────────────────────
+        elif key in (KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_FY, KEY_MATERIAL_CROSS_BRACING_FY, KEY_MATERIAL_END_DIAPHRAGM_FY):
             v = self._to_float(inputs.get(key))
@@
-        elif key == KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_FU:
+        elif key in (KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_FU, KEY_MATERIAL_CROSS_BRACING_FU, KEY_MATERIAL_END_DIAPHRAGM_FU):
@@
-        elif key == KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_E:
+        elif key in (KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_E, KEY_MATERIAL_CROSS_BRACING_E, KEY_MATERIAL_END_DIAPHRAGM_E):
@@
-        elif key == KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_G:
+        elif key in (KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_G, KEY_MATERIAL_CROSS_BRACING_G, KEY_MATERIAL_END_DIAPHRAGM_G):
@@
-        elif key == KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_POISSON:
+        elif key in (KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_POISSON, KEY_MATERIAL_CROSS_BRACING_POISSON, KEY_MATERIAL_END_DIAPHRAGM_POISSON):
@@
-        elif key == KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_THERMAL:
+        elif key in (KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_THERMAL, KEY_MATERIAL_CROSS_BRACING_THERMAL, KEY_MATERIAL_END_DIAPHRAGM_THERMAL):
@@
-        if key == KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_DENSITY:
+        if key in (KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_DENSITY, KEY_MATERIAL_CROSS_BRACING_DENSITY, KEY_MATERIAL_END_DIAPHRAGM_DENSITY):
(Confirm intended limits per component/spec before applying; adjust messages to be component-aware if desired.)
Duplicate check
Searched refreshed issues (open+closed, PRs skipped, notes/issues_raw.json through #126) via scripts/search_issues.py: cross_bracing.fy / end_diaphragm.fy — no direct matches; #118 (cross-field consistency fu<fy, G vs E,ν) different scope; #43/#125 (storage/consumption/staleness of CB/ED custom materials) different scope; #96 (OSI load skips material validation) related but different path. No duplicate found.
Notes
Related behavior areas (not claimed as this bug): dialog per-field checks/cross-field consistency (#118, #76), CB/ED custom grade consumption (#43), stale custom material state (#125), OSI load-time material validation gap (#96).

title: # [Docs/Examples] `example_basic.yaml` uses placeholder keys but passes `validate_osi_inputs` vacuously
body:
**Environment**
- OsdagBridge `dev` @ `d74f56d` (2026-07-26)
- macOS (Intel), conda env `osdagbridge-env`, Python 3.12.16
- Finding type: **T7 (oddity/misleading example; validator behavior may be intentional)**

**Description**
`examples/plate_girder/example_basic.yaml` contains a placeholder schema (e.g. `project.span_m`) rather than the real dotted OSI input keys used by the application (e.g. `geometry.span`, `geometry.carriageway_width`, `geometry.skew_angle`). Despite not providing those real inputs, it passes `validate_osi_inputs` with no errors/warnings because the validator only polices values for *present* known keys and does not require basic inputs to be present at load.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Open/parse `examples/plate_girder/example_basic.yaml` from the source tree (`dev @ d74f56d`).
2. Run OSI validation on the loaded data (`validate_osi_inputs`).

**Observed behavior (evidence)**
- Top-level key: `['project']` (no real dotted input keys such as `geometry.span` / `geometry.carriageway_width` / `geometry.skew_angle`)
- `validate_osi_inputs` result: `is_valid=True`, `errors=[]`, `warnings=[]`

(Recorded in `evidence/logs/phase1_examples.txt`; `tests/test_phase1_packaging.py::test_examples_parse_and_validate` confirms current state.)

**Expected behavior**
An illustrative/basic example would typically use the actual OSI key schema so users can load/adapt it meaningfully. Alternatively, if placeholder examples are intentional, they should be clearly labeled as non-loadable templates and/or validation/documentation should make their status explicit.

**Actual behavior**
The shipped example uses a non-real placeholder schema yet is accepted by the OSI loader/validator vacuously, which can be misleading.

**Impact**
- Users may assume `example_basic.yaml` is a valid, usable input example when it does not specify the required/real input keys.
- Can cause confusion when adapting the example for actual design runs.

**Suggested fix**
- Replace/update `example_basic.yaml` to use real dotted OSI keys and representative valid values, **or**
- Clearly mark it as a conceptual placeholder (not a loadable input) and/or adjust documentation/validation messaging so its non-runnable nature is explicit.

**Duplicate check**
Searched existing OsdagBridge issues (open+closed, full titles/bodies, refreshed `notes/issues_raw.json` through #126) for `example_basic` / placeholder-key example terms — no matching issue found. (Related load/validation issues like #19/#67/#69/#88/#96 concern different behaviors.)

**Notes**
This is reported as **T7** because the validator’s tolerant “validate only present known keys” behavior may be intentional; the shipped example content is nonetheless potentially misleading.

title: environment.yml missing PySide6, navcube, and osdag>=2026.04.0.0 causing startup and Stage 7 ModuleNotFoundError
body:
Creating a fresh Conda environment directly from the repository's `environment.yml` (`conda env create -f environment.yml`) fails to launch the desktop GUI and subsequently crashes during Stage 7 (`_stage_transverse_design`) due to missing or outdated dependencies:
1. **Missing `PySide6`:** Launching `python -m osdagbridge.desktop` fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'PySide6'` in `src/osdagbridge/desktop/__main__.py` (line 75).

3. **Outdated `osdag` Package (`osdag_core` Missing):** `environment.yml` resolves `osdag::osdag` to `2025.01.a.2-py_0`, which lacks `osdag_core`, causing `ensure_osdag_core_db()` (`src/osdagbridge/desktop/__main__.py`, line 214) to log an error on startup and crashing Stage 7 (`src/osdagbridge/core/utils/connect.py`, line 31) during cross-bracing design.

- **Python Version:** 3.12.16 (`osdagbridge-env`)

title: Stale girder segment_table end lengths and custom material properties persist in input_dict across consecutive design runs
body:
### **Description**

When executing multiple sequential design runs in the same desktop session (unlocking inputs, changing the span, girder count, or materials, and re-running **Design**), stale values from earlier runs remain inside the internal `input_dict` and exported `.osi` file:
1. **Stale Girder Segment Lengths (`segment_table`):** After changing **Span** from `20 m` to `25 m` and increasing **No. of Girders** from `3` to `4`, girders `G2` and `G3` retained their old `end: 20.0` length from the earlier run, whereas girders `G0`, `G1`, and `G4` updated to `25.0`.
2. **Stale Custom Materials:** After switching **Girder** and **Deck** back to standard grades (`E 250A` and `M35`), **Cross Bracing** and **End Diaphragm** retained the custom steel material (`custom_steel_626_1500`) from an earlier run.

### Environment
- **OS:** macOS (Apple Silicon `osx-arm64`)
- **Python Version:** 3.12.16 (`osdagbridge-env`)
- **Repository / Branch:** `Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge` (`dev` branch)

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Launch `python -m osdagbridge.desktop` and select a valid **Project Location** (e.g., `Rohtak, Haryana`).
2. Run Design #1 with **Span (m)** = `20.0`, **Carriageway Width (Each way) (m)** = `4.25`, and default `3` girders.
3. Unlock inputs, create and apply a custom steel material (`custom_steel_626_1500`), set **Span (m)** = `30.0`, **Carriageway Width (Each way) (m)** = `7.5`, and run Design #2.
4. Unlock inputs, set **Span (m)** = `25`, **Carriageway Width (Each way) (m)** = `10.5`, change **Girder** to `E 250A` and **Deck** to `M35`, open **Additional Inputs -> Typical Section Details**, set **No. of Girders** = `4`, click **Save**, and run Design #3.
5. Click **Save Input** to export the `.osi` file and inspect `member_properties.girder_details.segment_table`.

### Expected Behaviour
Whenever `geometry.span` or `typical_section.no_of_girders` is modified and **Design** is re-executed, all active girder entries (`G1` through `G4`) in `member_properties.girder_details.segment_table` should update their `end` coordinate to match the active span (`25.0 m`).

### Actual Behaviour
Exported `.osi` dictionary contains mismatched girder segment lengths (`G2` and `G3` retain `end: 20.0` from Design #1):

```yaml
member_properties.girder_details.segment_table.G1:
- end: 25.0
  id: G1M1
  start: 0.0
member_properties.girder_details.segment_table.G2:
- end: 20.0
  id: G2M1
  start: 0.0
member_properties.girder_details.segment_table.G3:
- end: 20.0
  id: G3M1
  start: 0.0
member_properties.girder_details.segment_table.G4:
- end: 25.0
  id: G4M1
  start: 0.0

title: Inconsistent Overall Bridge Width displayed across 3D CAD overlay (25.45 m), Results Table (26.65 m), and saved .osi dictionary (26.85 m)
body:
For the exact same bridge configuration with median and footpaths enabled, three different modules report three different values for **Overall Bridge Width**:
1. **3D CAD Viewport Info Overlay:** Displays `25.45 m`
2. **Generated Results Table (`Bridge Configuration Summary`):** Exports `26.65 m`
3. **Saved `.osi` Input Dictionary (`typical_section.overall_bridge_width`):** Stores `26.85 m` (`26.849999999999998`)

### Environment
- **OS:** macOS (Apple Silicon `osx-arm64`)
- **Python Version:** 3.12.16 (`osdagbridge-env`)
- **Repository / Branch:** `Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge` (`dev` branch)

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Launch `python -m osdagbridge.desktop`.
2. Select a valid **Project Location** (e.g., `Rohtak, Haryana`).
3. Enter:
   - **Span (m):** `25`
   - **Carriageway Width (Each way) (m):** `10.5`
   - **Include Median:** `Yes`
   - **Footpath:** `Both Sides`
   - **Skew Angle (deg):** `10`
   - **Design Type:** `Optimized`
4. Open **Additional Inputs -> Typical Section Details**, set `No. of Girders = 4`, click **Save**, and click **Design**.
5. Compare the bottom-left 3D CAD overlay, **Output Dock -> Generate Results Table -> Bridge Configuration Summary**, and the saved `.osi` file (`Save Input`).

### Expected Behaviour
All three outputs (3D CAD overlay, Results Table, and `input_dict["typical_section.overall_bridge_width"]`) should display the exact same overall bridge width (`26.85 m`).

### Actual Behaviour
- **3D CAD Info Overlay:** Shows `Overall Bridge Width: 25.45 m` (omits outer railings/barriers).
- **Results Table (`Bridge Configuration Summary`):** Shows `Overall Width (m): 26.65` (uses `railing.width = 0.275 m`).
- **Saved `.osi` Dictionary:** Stores `typical_section.overall_bridge_width: 26.849999999999998` (`typical_section.railing.width: 0.375`).

### Root Cause
In `src/osdagbridge/desktop/ui/cad_3d.py` (`CAD3DWindow.update_info_table`, lines 560–572), the overlay reads `model_data["total_deck_width"]` from `src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_components/super_structure/deck/builder.py` (line 388, `calculate_deck_width(...)`), which excludes outer railing width, rather than reading `KEY_TS_OVERALL_WIDTH` (`typical_section.overall_bridge_width`) computed by `CrossSectionLayout.total_width` in `src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/initial_sizing.py` (lines 135–160):

```python
# src/osdagbridge/desktop/ui/cad_3d.py (lines 560-563)
model_data = getattr(self.generator, "model_data", None)
if model_data and "total_deck_width" in model_data:
    bridge_width_mm = model_data["total_deck_width"]

### Suggested Fix
Unify the overall bridge width source so CAD3DWindow.update_info_table() and generate_results_values_builder.py both read the canonical typical_section.overall_bridge_width value (converted to mm where needed) and synchronize typical_section.railing.width (0.375 m) across sizing and report builders:
```

# In src/osdagbridge/desktop/ui/cad_3d.py (update_info_table)
overall_width_m = getattr(params, "overall_bridge_width", None)
if overall_width_m is not None:
    bridge_width_mm = overall_width_m * 1000.0
elif model_data and "total_deck_width" in model_data:
    bridge_width_mm = model_data["total_deck_width"]
```

title: [Bug/Database] Save Inputs and Save Outputs CSV Menu Actions Are Not Connected
body: ## Description The Database menu contains two CSV export options: `Save Inputs (.csv)` and `Save Outputs (.csv)`. However, neither QAction is connected to an export handler. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Launch OsdagBridge. 2. Open the Database menu. 3. Click `Save Inputs (.csv)`. 4. Observe that no save dialog or exported file appears. 5. Repeat with `Save Outputs (.csv)`. ## Expected Behaviour Both actions should export their respective dictionaries to CSV and allow the user to select a destination. ## Actual Behaviour Both menu items are visible but clicking them performs no action. ## Source Evidence

title: [Bug] Chapter 3 merged live load table conflates vehicle axle loads and pedestrian footway loadings
body:
### Summary
In `src/osdagbridge/core/reports/chap3.py`, vehicle live loads (IRC Class A / 70R) and pedestrian footpath live loads are merged into a single table without distinguishing units (kN axle loads vs. kN/m² intensity) or design code clauses.

### Description
Per IRC 6:2017 Cl. 206, pedestrian footway loading is an area intensity (.0\text{ to }5.0\text{ kN/m}^2$, subject to reduction factors for effective span lengths $> 7.5\text{ m}$), whereas vehicle live loads represent discrete wheeled/tracked axle loads.
Merging both into a single generic table leads to ambiguity in units, load combinations, and design verification standards.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Configure a bridge with IRC Class A loading and pedestrian footpaths on both sides.
2. Generate Chapter 3 of the engineering design report.
3. Observe that footpath loadings are rendered inside the vehicle axle table without distinct intensity or reduction criteria.

### Suggested Fix
Split Chapter 3 into two dedicated tables:
- **Table 3.3**: Vehicle Live Loads (Vehicle Class, Bogie spacing, Axle loads, Impact factor, Braking/Traction)
- **Table 3.4**: Footpath and Pedestrian Live Loads (Footpath width, Design intensity per IRC 6:2017 Cl. 206.1, Reduction factor, Total applied load)

title: [Bug] Multi-page tables in design report omit \endhead, causing truncated column headers on continuation pages
body:
### Summary
Multi-page design check and material tables across Chapters 2, 3, 5, and 7 do not specify repeated table headers (`\endhead`), leaving continuation pages without column descriptions.

### Description
In multi-page LaTeX `longtable` environments, column headers must be terminated with `\endfirsthead` (for the initial page) and `\endhead` (for continuation pages).
In the current report generator, tables define their header rows once with `\hline` without header-repetition macros. When a table spans across 2 or 3 pages (e.g. Table 5.22, Table 7.1), subsequent pages display data rows directly below the page top margin without column designations, violating standard technical publishing conventions.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Generate a design report for a bridge model with all design checks enabled.
2. Compile to PDF or inspect generated `.tex` files.
3. Observe that continuation pages of multi-page check tables lack column labels.

### Suggested Fix
Wrap all multi-page tables with standardized `longtable` header blocks:
```latex
\endfirsthead
\multicolumn{N}{c}{{\bfseries \tablename\ \thetable{} -- Continued from previous page}} \\
\hline
... headers ...
\hline
\endhead
\hline
\multicolumn{N}{r}{{Continued on next page...}} \\
\endfoot
\hline
\endlastfoot
```

title: [Bug] Default 1-inch bottom margin causes check table content to overlap page footer rule
body:
### Summary
On multi-page design check tables (e.g. Girder G4 checks on Page 30), the default 1-inch bottom margin and 30pt footskip cause table rows and software-default footnotes to bleed directly into the bottom footer rule.

### Description
In `src/osdagbridge/core/reports/report_generator.py`, the LaTeX geometry package is configured with default 1-inch margins:
```latex
\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}
```
When multi-page check tables (Section 5.5) render detailed capacity evaluations with multi-line default footnotes, the available vertical clearance on the page is insufficient. This causes table border rules and trailing text to collide with the green footer rule box.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Configure a 4-girder bridge with span = 24m.
2. Run analysis and design check evaluation.
3. Generate report and inspect Page 30 / Girder G4 checks.
4. The final table row collides with the footer rule.

### Suggested Fix
Centralize document geometry settings in `styles.py` and expand the bottom margin to 2.8 cm with a footskip of 38 pt:
```latex
\usepackage[top=2.5cm, bottom=2.8cm, left=2.5cm, right=2.5cm, headheight=16pt, headsep=12pt, footskip=38pt]{geometry}
```

title: [Bug] Unclosed \begingroup in chap7.py leaks tabcolsep into subsequent report chapters
body:
### Summary
In `src/osdagbridge/core/reports/chap7.py`, a `\begingroup` is opened to constrain table column padding before `\begin{longtable}`, but no matching `\endgroup` is emitted after `\end{longtable}`.

### Description
In LaTeX, group scoping commands (`\begingroup` ... `\endgroup`) must be balanced. In `chap7.py`:
```latex
\begingroup
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3.5pt}
\begin{longtable}{...}
...
\end{longtable}
% Missing \endgroup here!
```
Because `\endgroup` is missing, the narrowed `\tabcolsep` setting leaks across the rest of the document, causing tables in Chapter 8 (Design Log) and Chapter 9 (References) to render with abnormally compressed column widths.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Generate an engineering design report including Chapters 7, 8, and 9.
2. Inspect the resulting `.tex` file or compile with `pdflatex`.
3. Observe that table column padding in Chapter 8 and 9 inherits the 3.5pt tabcolsep from Chapter 7.

### Suggested Fix
Add `\endgroup` immediately following the closing `\end{longtable}` statement in `chap7.py`.

title: [Bug] Custom material dialog accepts physically impossible combinations: fu < fy, and a shear modulus G that contradicts E and nu
body:
### What happens
The **Custom** material dialog (girder, cross-bracing or end-diaphragm steel) checks each field against its own range, one field at a time. It never checks the fields against each other, so it accepts and stores combinations that cannot exist. The custom steel then reaches the design.

### Environment
Windows 11 (Python 3.12.16, conda env from `environment.yml`), `dev` @ `d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3` (unmodified). Found and reproduced with my automated suite, which drives the real `MaterialPropertiesDialog._validate_and_save()` through the real `InputDock` material combo. Same results on a second, headless Linux run.

### Steps to reproduce (GUI)
1. Homepage > Girder material > **Custom...**
2. Enter fy **450**, fu **400**, leave the other fields at their defaults, press **Save**. It is accepted, and the combo now shows `custom_steel_450_400`.
3. Again **Custom...**: E 200, nu 0.3, G **120**, press **Save**. It is accepted with G = 120 GPa. With E = 200 and nu = 0.3, G must be E / (2(1 + nu)) = 76.9 GPa.

### Expected / actual
| Dialog entry | Expected | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| fy 450, fu 400 MPa | rejected (IS 2062: fu is always greater than fy) | **accepted** as `custom_steel_450_400` |
| E 200 GPa, nu 0.3, G 120 GPa | rejected, or G recomputed from E and nu | **accepted**, `material.girder.g = 120` |
| fy 410, fu 540 (normal) | accepted | accepted |
| density 130 kN/m³ / E 50 GPa | rejected (single-field range) | rejected |

It works for every single-field limit. It fails for any combination that is wrong only *relative to another field*. The stored values go into `input_dict` and reach the design: fy drives the girder checks, and fu drives rupture/connection checks.

### Evidence
Suite case U7, five dialog entries and the dialog's own verdict: [`checks.csv`](https://github.com/AdityaChauhanX07/OsdagBridge-Testing-Winter2026/blob/main/suite_runs/20261116_011421/checks.csv) (rows `U7`). From the run log on Windows 11:
```
FAIL U7 Custom steel fu < fy (450/400) rejected: expected reject  got accepted as custom_steel_450_400 (fy=450, fu=400, G=76.9)
FAIL U7 Custom steel G inconsistent with E,nu (E200, nu0.3, G 120) rejected: expected reject  got accepted as custom_steel_410_540 (fy=410, fu=540, G=120)
 ok  U7 Custom steel density 130 rejected
 ok  U7 Custom steel E 50 GPa rejected
```

### Root cause
* [`material_properties.py#L319-L355`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/desktop/ui/dialogs/material_properties.py#L319-L355) (`_validate_and_save`) loops over the fields and calls `self.validator.validate_material_inputs(key, {key: val})`, one field at a time.
* [`validator.py#L78-L172`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/validator.py#L78-L172) (`validate_material_inputs`) only has per-field range rules. There is no rule relating fu to fy, or G to E and nu.

### Suggested fix
Add one cross-field check to `BridgeInputValidator` and call it with all values at the end of `_validate_and_save()`. The `.osi` loader can reuse the same function.
```python
# validator.py (BridgeInputValidator)
def validate_material_consistency(self, v: dict) -> list[str]:
    errs = []
    fy, fu = self._to_float(v.get(KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_FY)), self._to_float(v.get(KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_FU))
    if fy is not None and fu is not None and fu <= fy:
        errs.append(f"Ultimate strength fu ({fu:g} MPa) must be greater than yield strength fy ({fy:g} MPa).")
    E, G, nu = (self._to_float(v.get(k)) for k in (KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_E, KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_G,
                                                    KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_POISSON))
    if None not in (E, G, nu) and abs(G - E / (2 * (1 + nu))) > 0.02 * G:
        errs.append(f"G must equal E / (2(1+nu)) = {E / (2 * (1 + nu)):.1f} GPa for E = {E:g} GPa, nu = {nu:g}.")
    return errs

# material_properties.py, end of _validate_and_save(), before self.accept()
values = {k: w.text().strip() for k, w in self.field_inputs.items()}
errors = self.validator.validate_material_consistency(values)
if errors:
    CustomMessageBox(title="Validation Error", text="\n".join(errors),
                     dialogType=MessageBoxType.Critical).exec()
    return
```
A simpler alternative for G is to make the field read-only and compute it from E and nu (the dialog's own defaults already follow that formula). Regression tests: fy 450 / fu 400, and G = 120 with E 200 / nu 0.3, are rejected; fy 410 / fu 540 / G 76.9 is accepted.

### Duplicate check
Checked all open/closed issues on 16 Nov 2026. #96 covers `.osi` **loading** skipping material validation; I add my design-run evidence there as a comment. #76 is about the number of decimals the dialog allows. Neither covers cross-field checks *inside the dialog*.

title: [Bug] Girder design uses the nominal yield strength for every plate thickness: 22 mm E 350 flanges designed with fy = 350 MPa instead of 330 MPa (IS 2062 Table 2)
body:
### What happens
IS 2062:2011 Table 2 gives a **thickness-dependent** minimum yield stress (E 350: 350 MPa for t < 20 mm, 330 MPa for 20-40 mm, 320 MPa for t > 40 mm; similar steps for every grade). IS 800 / IRC 22 require the value for the actual element thickness. OsdagBridge looks up one fy per grade and uses it for all plates, so any girder with a plate of 20 mm or more is designed with an over-estimated fy. This includes the default Optimized result for a 30 m span.

### Environment
Windows 11, Python 3.12, `dev` @ `d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3` (unmodified). Also reproduced headlessly on Linux.

### Steps to reproduce
Homepage: span 30 m, carriageway 7.5 m, Optimized, girder steel **E 350A**. Design. `design_results.tf_top_mm = 22.0`, `tf_bot_mm = 22.0`, `fy_MPa = 350.0`.

### Expected / actual
| Plate | Thickness | fy used | fy per IS 2062 Table 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Top/bottom flange | 22 mm | 350 MPa | **330 MPa** |
| Web | 10 mm | 350 MPa | 350 MPa |

The flange-governed capacities (plastic moment, LTB, flange classification epsilon = sqrt(250/fy)) are therefore about 6% too high for this default design. It is correct only when every plate is under 20 mm. Thicker flanges, larger spans and custom thicknesses all get an un-reduced fy (a 45 m span, or a 40 mm flange, would need 320 MPa).

### Evidence
* GUI run on Windows: [`gui_runs/TC00_baseline/run01_output.json`](https://github.com/AdityaChauhanX07/OsdagBridge-Testing-Winter2026/blob/main/gui_runs/TC00_baseline/run01_output.json), keys `design_results.fy_MPa`, `tf_top_mm`, `tw_mm`.
* Suite: [`runs.csv`](https://github.com/AdityaChauhanX07/OsdagBridge-Testing-Winter2026/blob/main/suite_runs/20261116_011421/runs.csv) columns `fy_used_MPa`, `tf_mm` (check C11 "Design fy = girder material fy" is reported as INFO for every run, with flanges of 22 mm and more).
* Note that `osdag_core`, which OsdagBridge already depends on for the bracing member design, stores the three thickness bands in its `Material` table (`E 350 (Fe 490)`: 350 / 330 / 320). OsdagBridge's own `Steel_Grade_Properties` table has a single `Yield Strength` column.

### Root cause
* [`plategirderbridge.py#L1196-L1199`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/plategirderbridge.py#L1196-L1199): `fy = self._lookup_material(steel_grade, "Yield Strength")`, one value per grade from `Steel_Grade_Properties`.
* [`designer.py#L281-L282`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/designer.py#L281-L282): `fy_struct = steel_prop.Fy / 1e6` is used for all girder checks, whatever the plate thickness.

### Suggested fix
Resolve fy from the governing plate thickness:
```python
# core/utils/codes/is2062_2011.py (new)
_FY_BANDS = {"E 250": (250, 240, 230), "E 275": (275, 265, 255), "E 300": (300, 290, 280),
             "E 350": (350, 330, 320), "E 410": (410, 390, 380), "E 450": (450, 430, 420),
             "E 550": (550, 530, 520), "E 600": (600, 580, 570), "E 650": (650, 630, 620)}

def fy_for_thickness(grade: str, t_mm: float) -> float:
    m = re.match(r"\s*E\s*(\d+)", grade)                   # "E 350A", "E 250B0" -> "E 350", "E 250"
    lt20, t20_40, gt40 = _FY_BANDS[f"E {m.group(1)}"]
    return lt20 if t_mm < 20 else (t20_40 if t_mm <= 40 else gt40)

# designer.py, after the section is resolved
fy_flange = fy_for_thickness(steel_grade, max(sec.tf_top, sec.tf_bot))
fy_web    = fy_for_thickness(steel_grade, sec.tw)
material.fy = min(fy_flange, fy_web)    # conservative single value; or pass fy_flange/fy_web separately
```
Custom grades keep the user's fy (and should ask for the thickness bands, or state that the value applies to all thicknesses). Regression test: E 350A with tf = 22 mm gives `fy_MPa == 330`, and with tf = 16 mm gives 350.

### Duplicate check
Checked all open/closed issues on 15 Nov 2026. #95 is about how the stress limit is displayed (0.9 fy vs fy/gamma_m0). #42 is about Gs for E 350A. No issue on thickness-dependent fy.

title: [Bug] Optimized mode: analysis, self-weight and BOM use the un-rounded initial-sizing section (A = 34,919 mm²), while the design check uses the rounded plates (A = 38,700 mm², +10.8%)
body:
### What happens
In Optimized mode with thickness "All" (the default), the plate thicknesses are rounded up to standard SAIL plates before design (tf 21.25 -> 22 mm, tw 8.137 -> 10 mm). The section **properties** (A, Iz, Iy, It, Iw, Z, mass) and the web depth are not recomputed. So the grillage stiffness, the girder self-weight load and the bill of materials describe one girder, while the IRC 22 checks and the CAD use a different, 10.8% heavier one.

### Environment
Windows 11, Python 3.12, `dev` @ `d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3` (unmodified). Also reproduced headlessly on Linux.

### Steps to reproduce
Homepage: span 30 m, carriageway 7.5 m, **Optimized**, defaults (thicknesses "All"). Design. Compare `design_results` with the girder section-property keys and the self-weight line in the log.

### Expected / actual (TC00, one run)
| Quantity | Used by analysis / self-weight / BOM (input dict) | Used by design check (`design_results`) |
|---|---|---|
| Top/bottom flange thickness | 21.25 mm (initial sizing) | **22 mm** |
| Web thickness | 8.137 mm | **10 mm** |
| Web depth | 1628 mm | 1626 mm (= 1670 - 2 x 22) |
| Area | `section_properties.area.G1.M1` = 0.03491878 m² | `A_steel_mm2` = **38,700** mm² (+10.8%) |
| Iz | 0.0176543 m⁴ | `Iz_steel_mm4` = 1.882e10 mm⁴ (+6.6%) |
| Girder self-weight | log: `2741.12 N/m (A=0.03492 m²)` | 38,700 mm² x 78.5 kN/m³ = 3038 N/m |

Expected: one section everywhere. The mismatch appears in every Optimized run of the suite (check C10 in [`checks.csv`](https://github.com/AdityaChauhanX07/OsdagBridge-Testing-Winter2026/blob/main/suite_runs/20261116_011421/checks.csv); every girder count and span tested). Manual mode is not affected, because there the entered thicknesses are used for both.

### Evidence
* GUI run on Windows: [`gui_runs/TC00_baseline/run01_output.json`](https://github.com/AdityaChauhanX07/OsdagBridge-Testing-Winter2026/blob/main/gui_runs/TC00_baseline/run01_output.json) and [`session.log`](https://github.com/AdityaChauhanX07/OsdagBridge-Testing-Winter2026/blob/main/gui_runs/TC00_baseline/session.log) (self-weight line). Suite: [`runs.csv`](https://github.com/AdityaChauhanX07/OsdagBridge-Testing-Winter2026/blob/main/suite_runs/20261116_011421/runs.csv) columns `sw_area_m2` vs `A_steel_check_m2`.
* The report's bill of materials for the steel girders uses the stale area (32.89 t for 4 x 30 m, against about 36.4 t for the designed plates).

### Root cause
`design()` calls [`_resolve_optimized_bounds_to_mm()`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/plategirderbridge.py#L450) ([`L682`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/plategirderbridge.py#L682)). It snaps the thickness keys `"All"` to the next SAIL plate but only rewrites the **dimension** keys. The **property** keys written earlier by the Additional Inputs compute functions from the initial-sizing dimensions are left untouched. `_girder_section()` then builds the grillage section (and the self-weight area) from those stale property keys ([`L1260-L1277`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/plategirderbridge.py#L1260-L1277): `A=g(KEY_MP_GIRDER_SECTIONAL_AREA)`, `Iz=g(KEY_MP_GIRDER_SECTIONAL_IZ)`, ...). The designer recomputes A/I from the snapped dimensions.

### Suggested fix
After the dimensions are resolved, recompute the properties from them, once, per girder:
```python
# plategirderbridge.py, end of _resolve_optimized_bounds_to_mm() (or start of _build_dtos())
from osdagbridge.core.bridge_types.plate_girder.initial_sizing import BridgeConfigurationSolver
span = float(self.input_dict[KEY_SPAN])
solver = self._layout_solver()      # BridgeConfigurationSolver built as in solve_extend_basic_input_dict()
for i in range(self._girder_count()):
    sfx = f".G{i+1}.M1"
    v = lambda k: self._girder_value(k, i)          # metres after _convert_girder_dims_mm_to_m()
    p = solver.compute_section_properties(
            span=span, symmetry=v(KEY_MP_GIRDER_SYMMETRY),
            user_depth=v(KEY_MP_GIRDER_DEPTH),
            B_top=v(KEY_MP_GIRDER_TOP_FLANGE_WIDTH), B_bot=v(KEY_MP_GIRDER_BOTTOM_FLANGE_WIDTH),
            t_f_top=v(KEY_MP_GIRDER_TOP_FLANGE_THICKNESS), t_f_bot=v(KEY_MP_GIRDER_BOTTOM_FLANGE_THICKNESS),
            t_w=v(KEY_MP_GIRDER_WEB_THICKNESS))
    self.input_dict.update({
        KEY_MP_GIRDER_WEB_DEPTH + sfx:      p["d_web"],
        KEY_MP_GIRDER_SECTIONAL_AREA + sfx: p["Area"],
        KEY_MP_GIRDER_SECTIONAL_IZ + sfx:   p["I_z"],
        KEY_MP_GIRDER_SECTIONAL_IY + sfx:   p["I_y"],
        KEY_MP_GIRDER_MASS + sfx:           p["Mass"],
        # ... Z_ez / Z_pz / r_z / r_y / It / Iw keys likewise
    })
```
(`compute_section_properties()` in [`initial_sizing.py#L424`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/initial_sizing.py#L424) already returns these quantities in metres.) Regression test: Optimized TC00 must give `section_properties.area.G1.M1 * 1e6 == design_results["A_steel_mm2"]`, and a self-weight line load equal to A x density.

### Duplicate check
Checked all open/closed issues on 15 Nov 2026. #90 is about Optimized-mode **constraints** (allowed thickness lists and bounds) being ignored. This issue is about the **properties** not following the chosen plates. #20 covers the density value, not the area. #103 reports the Material Take-off using G1's area for every girder; the stale-area root cause here also explains part of that bill-of-materials mismatch, but the analysis/self-weight inconsistency is not covered there.

title: [Bug] Deck cover check infers the exposure class from the concrete grade: upgrading M40 -> M45/M50 switches to "Extreme" exposure, requires 75 mm cover and fails the deck
body:
### What happens
The deck design never asks for the exposure condition. It **derives** the exposure from the concrete grade: it picks "the most severe exposure the grade satisfies". So a better concrete makes the software assume a harsher environment and demand more cover:

| Deck concrete | Exposure assumed | Min. cover required | Provided (default) | Report "Clear Cover" row |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M40 (default) | Very Severe | 50 mm | 50 mm | PASS |
| M45 | **Extreme** | **75 mm** | 50 mm | **FAIL** |
| M50 | **Extreme** | **75 mm** | 50 mm | **FAIL** |
| custom `custom_concrete_45_3.8` (fck 45) | **Extreme** | **75 mm** | 50 mm | **FAIL** |

The same bridge at the same site passes with M40 and fails with M45. The opposite should happen: IRC 112 Table 14.2 gives the *minimum* grade and cover for a given exposure, so a higher grade can only help. The cover result is also not part of any deck status flag. Only the text and the report row show it, so the overall status ignores it. (The executive summary's "Deck design pass" text is the hard-coded summary already reported in #65.)

### Environment
Windows 11, Python 3.12, `dev` @ `d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3` (unmodified). Also reproduced headlessly on Linux.

### Steps to reproduce (GUI)
1. Homepage: span 30 m, carriageway 7.5 m, Optimized, deck concrete **M40**. Design, then generate the report: deck "Clear Cover (IRC 112 Cl. 15.2)" is `>= 50 mm (Table 14.2) ... PASS`.
2. Unlock, change only the deck concrete to **M45**, Design and generate the report: `>= 75 mm (Table 14.2) | Top 50 / Bottom 50 mm | FAIL`. The deck design text says `Concrete grade : M45 -> Exposure: Extreme ... Top cover provided : 50 mm -> BELOW RECOMMENDED`.

### Evidence
* Suite case S10 (M45, M50) vs baseline M40: [`S10_deck_grade/`](https://github.com/AdityaChauhanX07/OsdagBridge-Testing-Winter2026/tree/main/suite_runs/20261116_011421/S10_deck_grade) (`deck_design_results.deck_exposure`, `min_cover_recommended`, full deck text in the output dict). Check D1 in [`checks.csv`](https://github.com/AdityaChauhanX07/OsdagBridge-Testing-Winter2026/blob/main/suite_runs/20261116_011421/checks.csv).
* GUI run with custom fck 45 on Windows: [`gui_runs/TC01_custom_materials/report/TC01_report.tex`](https://github.com/AdityaChauhanX07/OsdagBridge-Testing-Winter2026/blob/main/gui_runs/TC01_custom_materials/report/TC01_report.tex) L1745 (`>= 75 mm ... FAIL`). The M40 run [`TC00_report.tex`](https://github.com/AdityaChauhanX07/OsdagBridge-Testing-Winter2026/blob/main/gui_runs/TC00_baseline/report/TC00_report.tex) L1745 shows `>= 50 mm ... PASS`.

### Root cause
[`irc112_2019.py#L108-L145`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/utils/codes/irc112_2019.py#L108-L145):
```python
chosen = IRC112_2019._TABLE_14_2[0]
for row in IRC112_2019._TABLE_14_2:      # Moderate(25,40) Severe(30,45) Very Severe(40,50) Extreme(45,75)
    if fck_val >= row[3]:                # row[3] = minimum grade for that exposure
        chosen = row                     # -> most severe exposure the grade "satisfies"
```
`deckdesign.py` calls it with the grade only ([`L493-L496`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/deckdesign.py#L493-L496)). `cover_top_ok / cover_bot_ok` only reach the text and report table, not any status flag that the summary uses.

### Suggested fix
Make exposure an input (Additional Inputs > Design Options > Deck, default "Severe" or "Very Severe" for bridge decks) and look the table up **by exposure**. Then check the chosen grade against that row:
```python
@staticmethod
def table_14_2_min_cover(exposure: str, concrete_grade: str) -> dict:
    row = next(r for r in IRC112_2019._TABLE_14_2 if r[0] == exposure)
    fck = int(re.findall(r"\d+", concrete_grade)[0])
    return {"exposure_condition": row[0], "min_cover_mm": row[4], "min_grade_MPa": row[3],
            "grade_ok": fck >= row[3], ...}
```
In `deckdesign.py`, add `cover_top_ok`, `cover_bot_ok` and `grade_ok` to the deck pass/fail status (for example a `deck_status` key next to `deck_exposure`), so that the overall status can use it. Regression test: with the same exposure, M40 -> M45 must not increase the required cover, and a cover shortfall must give a deck FAIL status.

### Duplicate check
Checked all open/closed issues on 15 Nov 2026. #65 covers the hard-coded "design pass" summary text. No issue on how the deck exposure/cover is chosen.

title: [Bug] Two different girder deflections for the same run: design check 22.87 mm (PASS) vs per-girder output/report 51.23 mm (FAIL vs L/600 = 50 mm)
body:
### What happens
Every run produces two sets of deflections that differ by the composite stiffness ratio (about 2.2x). The DCR/design check uses one set and the per-girder results (Generate Results dialog, output dictionary, report Table 5.10 and chapter 4) use the other. For the default bridge, the design check reports SLS total deflection **PASS** while the report's per-girder table shows **FAIL** for the same girders.

### Environment
Windows 11, Python 3.12, `dev` @ `d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3` (unmodified). Also reproduced headlessly on Linux.

### Steps to reproduce
Homepage: span 30 m, carriageway 7.5 m, skew 0, Optimized, defaults. **Design** and generate the report. Compare the DCR panel / report "SLS Deflection" check with report Table 5.10 (per-girder deflections), or compare these output-dictionary keys.

### Expected / actual (TC00, same run)
| Quantity | Design check (`design_results`, DCR panel, summary) | Per-girder output (`steeldesign.deflection.*.G1..G4`, report Table 5.10) | Limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total (DL + LL) | `delta_total_mm` = **22.871** -> PASS | G1 51.09, G2 **51.225**, G3 51.225, G4 51.09 -> **FAIL** | L/600 = 50.0 |
| Live load | `delta_live_mm` = 9.631 | 19.252 / 19.385 / 19.385 / 19.252 | L/800 = 37.5 |

The difference appears in every run of the automated suite (check C06). Two examples: span 20 m gives 21.52 vs 60.41 mm, and median + cw 15 m gives 50.82 vs 130.96 mm. The two values agree only in the skew cases, where the per-girder values are missing (see #89).

### Evidence
* TC00 GUI run on Windows: [`gui_runs/TC00_baseline/run01_output.json`](https://github.com/AdityaChauhanX07/OsdagBridge-Testing-Winter2026/blob/main/gui_runs/TC00_baseline/run01_output.json) (keys above) and the generated report [`report/TC00_report.pdf`](https://github.com/AdityaChauhanX07/OsdagBridge-Testing-Winter2026/blob/main/gui_runs/TC00_baseline/report/TC00_report.pdf) (deflection check PASS in the summary, FAIL in the per-girder table).
* Suite: [`runs.csv`](https://github.com/AdityaChauhanX07/OsdagBridge-Testing-Winter2026/blob/main/suite_runs/20261116_011421/runs.csv) columns `delta_total_check_mm` / `delta_total_output_max_mm` for 30 designs.

### Root cause
* The design check divides the grillage displacement by `stiffness_ratio = I_composite / I_steel` ([`designer.py#L2889`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/designer.py#L2889), applied at [`L2955`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/designer.py#L2955) and [`L2966`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/designer.py#L2966)).
* The per-girder values come from `build_deflections_cache()` ([`results_data.py#L768`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/results_data.py#L768)): raw grillage displacements, no correction. They are written to `steeldesign.deflection.total_mm.G*` in [`plategirderbridge.py#L779-L785`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/plategirderbridge.py#L779-L785), and the report reads exactly those keys ([`chap5.py#L466-L468`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/reports/chap5.py#L466-L468), [`chap4.py#L66`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/reports/chap4.py#L66)) and assigns PASS/FAIL against the limits.

So the same physical quantity goes through two different stiffness assumptions and reaches two different verdicts. (A single ratio for DL + LL is also questionable: steel + wet-concrete dead load acts on the bare steel section, and only superimposed dead load and live load act on the composite section.)

### Suggested fix
Compute the deflection once, per girder, in the designer, and write that same value everywhere:
```python
# designer.py, after computing per-girder values with the proper stiffness per load stage
dl_mm  = dy_dl_bare_steel_mm                      # stage 1: steel + wet concrete on I_steel
sdl_ll_mm = dy_sdl_ll_mm / stiffness_ratio        # stage 2: composite (short-term n for LL)
results.delta_total_mm = dl_mm + sdl_ll_mm
# plategirderbridge.py L779-785: write the designer's per-girder values, not the raw cache
for gi, r in design_results["per_girder"].items():
    self.output_dict[f"{KEY_SD_DEFL_TOTAL}.{gi}"] = r["demand"]["delta_total_mm"]
    self.output_dict[f"{KEY_SD_DEFL_LIVE}.{gi}"]  = r["demand"]["delta_live_mm"]
```
Alternatively, give the grillage longitudinal members the composite section for the SDL/LL cases, and drop the post-hoc division. Either way the DCR panel, the Generate Results dialog and both report tables must show one number. Regression test: assert `design_results["delta_total_mm"] == max(output["steeldesign.deflection.total_mm.G*"])` for TC00.

### Duplicate check
Checked all open/closed issues on 15 Nov 2026. #94 (check-card count) and #89 (skewed per-girder results) are different. No issue on the deflection mismatch.
