title: [Bug] Deck-edge grillage lines get the full plate-girder section and are designed as girders: 4-girder bridge is checked as 6 girders, per-girder self-weight moment = 0.67 x wL²/8
body:
### What happens
With a positive deck overhang (the default), the grillage has `n + 2` longitudinal lines: `n` girders plus the two deck-edge lines. The edge lines are given the **same plate-girder section** as the real girders, so they attract a full girder's share of the load. The design check then treats all `n + 2` lines as girders (`design_results.n_girders = 6`, `per_girder` G1-G6 for a 4-girder bridge). The real girders' demands come out too low (unconservative), and the girder labels no longer match the bridge.

### Environment
Windows 11, Python 3.12, `dev` @ `d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3` (unmodified). Also reproduced headlessly on Linux.

### Steps to reproduce
Homepage: span 30 m, carriageway 7.5 m, skew 0, Optimized, default materials (4 girders @ 2.1 m, overhang 1.05 m). Click **Design**. Inspect `design_results` in the output dictionary (or the per-girder tables in the report).

### Expected / actual (TC00)
* Self-weight is applied only on the 4 girder lines (log: `Self weight line load @ z=1.050 / 3.183 / 5.317 / 7.450 m: 2741.12 N/m`). A simply supported girder therefore needs M_SW = wL²/8 = 2.741 x 30² / 8 = **308.4 kNm**.
* Actual `per_girder[*].demand.M_girder_sw_kNm` = **206.16 / 205.42 / 205.18 / 205.18 / 205.42 / 206.16** kNm for **six** "girders". 6 x 205.4 = 4 x 308.4: the load is shared by 6 equal-stiffness lines instead of 4.
* `design_results.n_girders = 6`, `per_girder` keys G1-G6, while the input has `typical_section.no_of_girders = 4`. The output dock lists G1-G4 ([`output_dock.py#L830`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/desktop/ui/docks/output_dock.py#L830)) and looks results up by those labels. So "G1" in the dock is the deck-edge line, and the fourth real girder (line 5) cannot be selected.

The ratio follows n/(n+2) across all the girder counts the suite ran:

| Case (fresh session) | Girders | Lines checked | M_SW / (wL²/8) | n/(n+2) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| cw 4.25 m | 3 | 5 | 0.601 | 0.600 |
| TC00 cw 7.5 m | 4 | 6 | 0.669 | 0.667 |
| span 40 / cw 11 m | 5 | 7 | 0.714 | 0.714 |
| cw 20 then 11 m | 9 | 11 | 0.818 | 0.818 |
| cw 23.6 m | 10 | 12 | 0.859 | 0.833 |

It works only for zero overhang. Then `n_l = n` and the extreme lines are real girders (see #91 for the self-weight bug in that case).

### Evidence
Suite checks C01 (design-check girder count) and C05 (SW moment) fail in every positive-overhang run: [`SUMMARY.md`](https://github.com/AdityaChauhanX07/OsdagBridge-Testing-Winter2026/blob/main/suite_runs/20261116_011421/SUMMARY.md), [`checks.csv`](https://github.com/AdityaChauhanX07/OsdagBridge-Testing-Winter2026/blob/main/suite_runs/20261116_011421/checks.csv), [`runs.csv`](https://github.com/AdityaChauhanX07/OsdagBridge-Testing-Winter2026/blob/main/suite_runs/20261116_011421/runs.csv) (columns `n_girders_input`, `n_girders_checked`, `M_sw_ratio`). Example run with full dicts and log: [`S01_baseline_three_runs/run1_*`](https://github.com/AdityaChauhanX07/OsdagBridge-Testing-Winter2026/tree/main/suite_runs/20261116_011421/S01_baseline_three_runs). GUI run of the same inputs on Windows: [`gui_runs/TC00_baseline`](https://github.com/AdityaChauhanX07/OsdagBridge-Testing-Winter2026/blob/main/gui_runs/TC00_baseline).

### Root cause
1. [`plategirderbridge.py#L1006`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/plategirderbridge.py#L1006): `n_l = no_of_girders + 2` when overhang > 0 (fine). But [`L1113-L1118`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/plategirderbridge.py#L1113-L1118) passes `edge_longitudinal=self._girder_section()`, so the edge lines are modelled as full steel girders.
2. [`plategirderbridge.py#L2296`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/plategirderbridge.py#L2296) and [`L3765`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/plategirderbridge.py#L3765) build `PlateGirderAnalysisResults(dataset=..., bridge=...)` without `edge_dist`. The default `edge_dist=0` ([`analysis_results.py#L148`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/analysis_results.py#L148)) makes the naming at [`L455-L460`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/analysis_results.py#L455-L460) call the edge lines G1/G6 instead of EB1/EB2. The results cache built at [`L3290-L3294`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/plategirderbridge.py#L3290-L3294) already passes `edge_dist=self.get_edge_dist()`. That is why the per-girder deflections and plots show G1-G4 while the design check shows G1-G6 for the same run.
3. [`designer.py#L401`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/designer.py#L401): `n_girders = geom.n_l` (includes the edge lines; the comment at L407-L411 already notes that `_girder_count()` is the girder count). The exterior/interior classification at L412-L416 uses indices 0 and n_main-1 on the 6-line numbering, so it marks line G4 as "outer" and the real exterior girders (lines 2 and 5) as "inner".

### Suggested fix
```python
# plategirderbridge.py L1113-1118: model the deck-edge line as a slab strip, not as a girder
self.grillage_model.create_sections(
    girder_sections=girder_sections,
    edge_longitudinal=self._edge_slab_section(),   # new: deck strip of width = overhang, thickness = deck
    transverse=self._transverse_section(),
    end_transverse=self._end_transverse_section(),
)
# L2296 and L3765: tell the results object where the edge beams are
results = PlateGirderAnalysisResults(dataset=dataset, bridge=self.grillage_model,
                                     edge_dist=self.grillage_geometry.edge_dist)
# designer.py L401
n_girders = bridge._girder_count()
```
and iterate the per-girder checks over the `G1..Gn` members only (skip `EB1`/`EB2`). Regression test: TC00 must give `n_girders == 4`, per-girder M_SW close to wL²/8 (the slab-strip stiffness takes a little), and dock/report labels G1-G4 that match the per-girder results.

### Duplicate check
Checked all open/closed issues on 15 Nov 2026. #91 covers the zero-overhang case, where the outer **girders** are wrongly left without self-weight. This issue is the positive-overhang case, where the **deck edges** are wrongly modelled and designed as girders. Different trigger and different code path.

---
All scripts, inputs, outputs and logs: https://github.com/AdityaChauhanX07/OsdagBridge-Testing-Winter2026 (suite: `scripts/run_test_suite.py`, GUI logger: `scripts/run_logged.py`).

title: [Bug] Number of girders depends on the first carriageway width typed: same inputs give 3, 4, 5 or 9 girders (max DCR 1.13 to 1.69)
body:
### What happens
The girder layout (number of girders, spacing, overhang) is decided by the **first** carriageway width that triggers a layout solve in the session. It is never re-seeded when the carriageway width changes later. Two users who end up with identical homepage inputs therefore get different bridges and different design results. Typing a value, correcting it, unlocking and changing inputs after a run, or opening a file all lock in the old girder count.

### Environment
Windows 11 (Python 3.12.16, conda env from `environment.yml`), `dev` @ `d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3` (unmodified). Found and reproduced with my automated suite, which drives the real `InputDock`, Additional Inputs dialog and backend without source changes. The dict it builds matches the dict the real GUI sent on the same machine key for key (576 keys). Same results on a second, headless Linux run.

### Steps to reproduce (GUI)
1. Fresh start of the app. Location Mumbai, span 40, carriageway **11**. Open Additional Inputs > Typical Section: **5 girders @ 2.38 m**.
2. Restart the app. Location Mumbai, span 40, carriageway **20**, then change the carriageway to **11**. Open Additional Inputs > Typical Section: **9 girders @ 1.322 m**.
3. Restart. Carriageway 7.5 then 11 (or run Design at 7.5, unlock, change to 11): **4 girders @ 2.975 m**.

### Results (final homepage inputs identical: span 40 m, carriageway 11 m, skew 0, no median/footpath)
| How the value was entered | Girders | Spacing (m) | Overhang (m) | Design max DCR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 11 typed directly (fresh session) | **5** | 2.38 | 1.19 | **1.5115** |
| 7.5 typed first, corrected to 11 | 4 | 2.975 | 1.4875 | - |
| 5 typed first, corrected to 11 | 3 | 3.9667 | 1.9833 | - |
| 20 typed first, corrected to 11 | **9** | 1.3222 | 0.6611 | **1.1301** |
| Design at 7.5 m, unlock, change to span 40 / cw 11 | 4 | 2.975 | 1.4875 | **1.686** |

The layout works correctly only for the very first carriageway value of a session. Any later change keeps the old girder count and only re-spaces the girders.

### Evidence
* Suite case U2 (`U2_girder_count_table.json`) and design runs in S02 (`fresh_B`, `typo_B_cw20_then_11`, `run2_B`): [`suite_runs/.../S02_A_B_A`](https://github.com/AdityaChauhanX07/OsdagBridge-Testing-Winter2026/tree/main/suite_runs/20261116_011421/S02_A_B_A), with input/output dicts and logs. Summary in [`SUMMARY.md`](https://github.com/AdityaChauhanX07/OsdagBridge-Testing-Winter2026/blob/main/suite_runs/20261116_011421/SUMMARY.md), checks R4-R6.
* The suite drives the real `InputDock` widgets and `TemplatePage.update_cad_from_inputs()` logic, and its dict matches the real GUI dict key for key (check U1).

### Root cause
[`defaults.py#L915-L919`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/defaults.py#L915-L919):
```python
no_of_girders = int(
    basic_input_dict.get(KEY_TS_NO_OF_GIRDERS)
    or seed_no_of_girders(solver.calculate_overall_bridge_width())
)
sizing_result = solver._solve_layout(no_of_girders=no_of_girders, changed_field='girders')
```
`solve_extend_basic_input_dict()` runs after every required-field edit ([`template_page.py#L894-L897`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/desktop/ui/template_page.py#L894-L897), `update_cad_from_inputs`) and on Design / Load ([`L648`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/desktop/ui/template_page.py#L648), [`L867`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/desktop/ui/template_page.py#L867)). Once the first call has stored `KEY_TS_NO_OF_GIRDERS`, the seed from the new width is never used again, so the count reflects history, not the current inputs. (Many other keys are reset on the same call, see the Additional Inputs issue. The girder count is the opposite case: it is wrongly kept.)

### Suggested fix
Re-seed the count whenever the deck width changes, and keep a stored count only if the user set it explicitly in Typical Section:
```python
width = solver.calculate_overall_bridge_width()
user_n = basic_input_dict.get(KEY_TS_NO_OF_GIRDERS) if basic_input_dict.get("_ts_girders_user_set") else None
if user_n is None or basic_input_dict.get("_ts_layout_width") != width:
    user_n = seed_no_of_girders(width)
basic_input_dict["_ts_layout_width"] = width
no_of_girders = int(user_n)
```
(`_ts_girders_user_set` is set by the Typical Section girder-count handler and cleared when the carriageway/median/footpath changes.) Regression test: span 40 / cw 11 must give the same layout for the inputs "11", "7.5 then 11", "20 then 11", and after an unlock from a 7.5 m run.

### Duplicate check
Checked all open/closed issues on 15 Nov 2026. No issue on girder-count history. #71 and #86 concern values being **reset**; this one is a value being wrongly **kept**.

---

title: [Bug] Opening Additional Inputs and pressing Save (no edits) changes the design: LTB length jumps from 3 m to 15 m (Mb 7986 -> 2621 kNm)
body:
### What happens
With identical inputs, the girder LTB check, deck design and cross-bracing forces depend on whether the user ever opened the **Additional Inputs** dialog and pressed **Save**:

* Never opened (the normal "fill the homepage and click Design" path): the backend uses a hidden fallback cross-bracing spacing of **3.0 m**.
* Opened and saved with **no edits**: it uses **15.0 m**. This is the value the dialog shows (span / (No. of Cross Bracings + 1) = 30/(1+1)), and the value the design report prints in Table 2.7 in **both** cases.

So in the default path the design report says 15 m, but the LTB check assumed 3 m. That makes the Stage-2 LTB capacity 3x higher than for the spacing shown to the user (unconservative).

### Environment
Windows 11 (Python 3.12.16, conda env from `environment.yml`), `dev` @ `d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3` (unmodified). Found and reproduced with my automated suite, which drives the real `InputDock`, Additional Inputs dialog and backend without source changes. The dict it builds matches the dict the real GUI sent on the same machine key for key (576 keys). Same results on a second, headless Linux run.

### Steps to reproduce (GUI)
1. Homepage: Mumbai, span 30 m, carriageway 7.5 m, skew 0, no median/footpath, Optimized, default materials. Click **Design**. Note the Stage 2 LTB result (DCR panel / report "Lateral-torsional buckling").
2. Unlock. Open **Additional Inputs**. Change nothing and press **Save**. Click **Design** again.
3. Compare the two runs.

### Expected / actual (same inputs, both runs)
| Output | Dialog never opened | Dialog opened + Save, no edits |
|---|---|---|
| `design_results.cross_bracing_spacing_m` | **3.0** | **15.0** |
| LTB note (check 6) | `LLT=cb_spacing=3.0m; lambda_LT=0.2992, chi_LT=1.0000` | `LLT=cb_spacing=15.0m; lambda_LT=1.4590, chi_LT=0.3282` |
| Stage 2 LTB capacity `Mb_kNm` | **7986.44** | **2621.07** |
| Stage 2 LTB DCR | 0.1505 | 0.4584 |
| Deck design "Cross-bracing spacing" / bottom bars | 3.000 m / Ø12 @ 175 | 15.000 m / Ø12 @ 185 |
| Report Table 2.7 "Spacing" | 15.0 m | 15.0 m |
| `member_properties.cross_bracing_details.spacing` (input dict) | `None` | `15.0` |

Works correctly only when the user happens to open and save the dialog. Fails (silently uses 3 m) in every session where the dialog is not saved, including after **Load Input** of an `.osi` saved without opening it.

### Evidence
* Suite case S11 vs the baseline run S01/run1 (same inputs): [`S11_open_additional_inputs_no_edit/`](https://github.com/AdityaChauhanX07/OsdagBridge-Testing-Winter2026/tree/main/suite_runs/20261116_011421/S11_open_additional_inputs_no_edit). `*_input.json` = exact dict sent to `set_input()`; `*_output.json.gz` = full output dict; `input_keys_changed_by_opening_dialog.json` = every key the dialog Save changed.
* Every baseline run in [`SUMMARY.md`](https://github.com/AdityaChauhanX07/OsdagBridge-Testing-Winter2026/blob/main/suite_runs/20261116_011421/SUMMARY.md) shows the 3 m fallback ([`checks.csv`](https://github.com/AdityaChauhanX07/OsdagBridge-Testing-Winter2026/blob/main/suite_runs/20261116_011421/checks.csv), check C09).

### Root cause
Every consumer reads only the un-suffixed key `KEY_MP_CB_SPACING` and falls back to 3.0 m when it is empty:
* [`designer.py#L404-L406`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/designer.py#L404-L406): LTB unbraced length (`LLT = cross_bracing_spacing_m`, used at L1805).
* [`crossbracingforces.py#L247-L251`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/crossbracingforces.py#L247-L251): `ai.get(KEY_MP_CB_SPACING) or 3.0  # TODO: remove fallback once UI always sets spacing`.
* [`deckdesign.py#L472`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/deckdesign.py#L472): `float(inp.get(KEY_MP_CB_SPACING) or 3.0)`.

The un-suffixed key is written **only** by the Additional Inputs dialog when it saves (it is the form field of the currently selected girder pair). `solve_extend_basic_input_dict()` writes the per-pair keys `...spacing.G1G2.B1M1` = span/(n+1) = 15 m ([`defaults.py#L405-L432`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/defaults.py#L405-L432)), and the report prints those ([`chap2.py#L365`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/reports/chap2.py#L365)), but nothing in the analysis reads them. Separately, the grillage transverse lines ignore spacing altogether: `n_t = round(span / DEFAULT_CROSS_BRACING_SPACING * 2) + 1` ([`plategirderbridge.py#L1001`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/plategirderbridge.py#L1001)).

Side effect of the same dialog Save: girder section properties are written back as 3-significant-figure strings (`section_properties.area.G1.M1`: `0.03491878` -> `"3.49e-02"`, [`additional_inputs.py#L1441`](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/desktop/ui/dialogs/additional_input/additional_inputs.py#L1441)), so the self-weight area also changes (0.03492 -> 0.0349 m²).

### Suggested fix
1. Resolve spacing from one source that always exists, the per-pair keys `solve_extend_basic_input_dict()` already maintains, and remove the silent 3.0 fallbacks:
```python
# plategirderbridge.py (new helper)
def _cross_bracing_spacing(self, pair: str | None = None) -> float:
    """Spacing (m) for a girder pair 'G1G2'; governing (max) spacing if pair is None."""
    prefix = KEY_MP_CB_SPACING + "."
    vals = {k[len(prefix):].split(".")[0]: float(v) for k, v in self.input_dict.items()
            if k.startswith(prefix) and v not in (None, "")}
    if not vals:
        raise ValueError("Cross-bracing spacing missing: run solve_extend_basic_input_dict() first")
    return vals[pair] if pair else max(vals.values())
```
   Then `designer.py` L405: `cb_spacing = bridge._cross_bracing_spacing()` (the largest unbraced length governs LTB); `crossbracingforces.py` L250 and `deckdesign.py` L472 call the same helper instead of `... or 3.0`.
2. Build `n_t` in `_build_dtos()` from the resolved spacing (e.g. `n_t = max(3, round(span / spacing) * 2 + 1)`), so the grillage cross-frames are where the design assumes them.
3. In `AdditionalInputs`, keep full precision in the dict and format only the displayed text.
4. Regression test: TC00 inputs, `design()` with the dialog never opened vs opened and saved, must give identical `design_results`.

### Duplicate check
Checked all open/closed issues on 15 Nov 2026. #93 covers the **CAD** using the 3 m constant and says it has no effect on solver forces. This issue is about the **design/analysis** (LTB, deck, bracing forces) depending on dialog state. Not covered by #43, #71 or #86.

---
All scripts, inputs, outputs and logs: https://github.com/AdityaChauhanX07/OsdagBridge-Testing-Winter2026 (suite: `scripts/run_test_suite.py`, GUI logger: `scripts/run_logged.py`).

title: [Bug] Material Take-off prices top/bottom bracing chords with the diagonal's area and reads only the G1-G2 bracing section
body: ### Summary The bracing rows of the Material Take-off use a single section area, read from the G1-G2 diagonal, for the top chords, bottom chords and diagonals of every bay. The chord sections and the sections of the other girder pairs, which the design computes and the report prints, are never read. ### Description `calculate_material_quantities` (`src/osdagbridge/core/boq/boq_generator.py`) reads one value, `transverse_member_design.cb.section_properties.bracing.G1G2.A`, and uses it for the top chord, bottom chord and diagonal quantities in all bays. The design selects the diagonal and the chord section separately for each girder pair (`diag_des` and `chord_des`, `plategirderbridge.py:2403-2425`) and stores their properties under separate `bracing`, `top_chord` and `bottom_chord` keys per pair (`plategirderbridge.py:2447-2527`). The report's cross-bracing table reads them separately (`chap5.py:714-720`). **Works:** the diagonal weight follows the G1-G2 diagonal area. **Fails:** (1) the chord weights follow the diagonal's area, not the chord's own. (2) Sections for G2-G3 and later pairs are ignored. ### Expected vs actual | | Expected | Actual | |---|---|---| | Top and bottom chord weight | Uses the chord section area | Uses the diagonal section area | | Bays other than G1-G2 | Use their own pair's sections | Use the G1-G2 diagonal area | ### Reproduction (no GUI, direct call) Synthetic `outputs`, using the key format the design writes (areas in cm²). Span 30 m, 4 girders, 3 m girder spacing, 5 m bracing spacing, 3.5 m diagonal. ```python from osdagbridge.core.boq import boq_generator as b P = "transverse_member_design.cb.section_properties." inp = {b.KEY_SPAN: 30.0, b.KEY_TS_NO_OF_GIRDERS: 4, b.KEY_TS_GIRDER_SPACING: 3.0} geom = {"crossbracing_forces_dict": {"geometry": {"diagonal_length_m": 3.5, "cb_spacing_m": 5.0}}} def run(diag_g1g2, chord_g1g2, diag_g2g3=None): out = dict(geom) out[P + "bracing.G1G2.A"] = diag_g1g2 out[P + "top_chord.G1G2.A"] = chord_g1g2 out[P + "bottom_chord.G1G2.A"] = chord_g1g2 if diag_g2g3 is not None: out[P + "bracing.G2G3.A"] = diag_g2g3 q = b.calculate_material_quantities(inp, out) return q["bracing_top_wt_total"], q["bracing_bot_wt_total"], q["bracing_diag_wt_total"] print("--- TEST C1: chord area changed, diagonal fixed (20 cm2)") for chord in (10.0, 40.0, 160.0): print("chord A =", chord, "cm2 -> top/bot/diag wt_total =", run(20.0, chord)) print("--- TEST C2: diagonal area changed, chord fixed (40 cm2)") for diag in (10.0, 20.0, 80.0): print("diag A =", diag, "cm2 -> top/bot/diag wt_total =", run(diag, 40.0)) print("--- TEST C3: G2G3 diagonal area changed (G1G2 fixed 20 cm2)") for d23 in (10.0, 80.0): print("G2G3 A =", d23, "cm2 ->", run(20.0, 40.0, d23)) ``` Output: ``` --- TEST C1: chord area changed, diagonal fixed (20 cm2) chord A = 10.0 cm2 -> top/bot/diag wt_total = ('0.71', '0.71', '1.65') chord A = 40.0 cm2 -> top/bot/diag wt_total = ('0.71', '0.71', '1.65') chord A = 160.0 cm2 -> top/bot/diag wt_total = ('0.71', '0.71', '1.65') --- TEST C2: diagonal area changed, chord fixed (40 cm2) diag A = 10.0 cm2 -> top/bot/diag wt_total = ('0.35', '0.35', '0.82') diag A = 20.0 cm2 -> top/bot/diag wt_total = ('0.71', '0.71', '1.65') diag A = 80.0 cm2 -> top/bot/diag wt_total = ('2.83', '2.83', '6.59') --- TEST C3: G2G3 diagonal area changed (G1G2 fixed 20 cm2) G2G3 A = 10.0 cm2 -> ('0.71', '0.71', '1.65') G2G3 A = 80.0 cm2 -> ('0.71', '0.71', '1.65') ``` What it shows: - **C1:** the chord weights do not change when the chord area changes 16×. - **C2:** the top and bottom chord weights scale with the diagonal area (0.35, 0.71, 2.83 for 10, 20 and 80 cm²). - **C3:** changing the G2-G3 section has no effect. Hand check for the 20 cm² case: 5 panels × 3 bays = 15 top-chord members × 0.002 m² × 3 m × 7.85 t/m³ = 0.71 t, and 30 diagonals × 0.002 m² × 3.5 m × 7.85 t/m³ = 1.65 t. Screenshot: This reproduction uses synthetic `outputs`. It has not been confirmed against a real design run where the chord section differs from the diagonal section. **Environment:** dev @ d74f56d (no upstream changes to `boq_generator.py` at time of testing), Windows, conda env `osdagbridge-env`. ### Root cause In `boq_generator.py`: ``` 246: bracing_area_val = outputs.get("transverse_member_design.cb.section_properties.bracing.G1G2.A") 288: top_chord_vol_single = bracing_area * spacing 301: bot_chord_vol_single = bracing_area * spacing 314: diag_vol_single = bracing_area * bracing_len ``` - One `bracing_area` is read at line 246 and reused for the top chord (line 288), bottom chord (line 301) and diagonals (line 314) in every bay. - `outputs` is read in this file only at lines 200-203, 246-247 and 271. The chord keys (`...top_chord.{pair}.A`, `...bottom_chord.{pair}.A`) and the keys for other pairs are never read, although `chap5.py:714-720` reads them for the report. - If the G1-G2 diagonal area, the diagonal length or the girder spacing is missing, line 270 turns all bracing rows into "N.A." without any error. Code at the tested commit: https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/boq/boq_generator.py#L246 https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/boq/boq_generator.py#L286-L317 ### Suggested approach (direction, not a drop-in; not yet run in the repo) Loop over the girder pairs and take each member's own area: ```python P = "transverse_member_design.cb.section_properties." def _cm2_to_m2(v): try: return float(v) / 1e4 except (TypeError, ValueError): return 0.0 top_vol = bot_vol = diag_vol = 0.0 for p in range(1, n_girders): pair = f"G{p}G{p + 1}" a_diag = _cm2_to_m2(outputs.get(P + f"bracing.{pair}.A")) a_top = _cm2_to_m2(outputs.get(P + f"top_chord.{pair}.A")) a_bot = _cm2_to_m2(outputs.get(P + f"bottom_chord.{pair}.A")) top_vol += n_panels * a_top * spacing bot_vol += n_panels * a_bot * spacing diag_vol += 2 * n_panels * a_diag * bracing_len # weights: volume * 7.85 (t/m3); the per-row "single" values and formula strings need adapting to show averages ``` The design gives both chords the same `chord_des` per pair (`plategirderbridge.py:2464-2466`), so the top and bottom areas are equal unless one chord is switched off. ### Related but distinct Other Material Take-off issues: #84 (crash-barrier row, unit mismatch), #102 (deck rebar and concrete rates) and #103 (steel girder volume). This issue covers the bracing rows. Also touching cross-bracing but not the take-off quantities: #93 (fixed cross-bracing spacing in the CAD) and #43 (custom cross-bracing grades unused in design).

title: fix(report): repeat table headers, add UR and material charts
body:
Six layout and maintainability fixes for the PDF design report:

1. Repeating table headers Every longtable now declares \endfirsthead/\endhead/\endfoot/ \endlastfoot, so the column header reappears after a page break. ensure_repeating_headers() applies the same treatment to tables that are still built as raw LaTeX strings, using the first \hline header \hline group as the header row.

2. Footer overlap and row height Tables keep a uniform row height (manual \\[6pt] row skips are normalised), page geometry reserves real space for the header and footer (headheight/headsep/footskip + includeheadfoot) and the body is \raggedbottom so the last row cannot be pushed into the footer. Per-girder group labels no longer use \multirow, which used to leak the next group's label below the table and into the footer.

3. Live loads split from footway loads Chapter 3 reports "Live Loads -- Vehicles (LL)" and "Live Loads -- Footway (LL)" as separate tables, each with an explicit Unit column; the footway table states explicitly when no footpath is configured.

4. Utilisation-ratio chart Section 5.5 embeds a bar chart (utilization ratio on the Y axis) built from exactly the rows of the UR summary table, with a horizontal red dashed capacity line at UR = 1.0 and failing elements in red.

5. Material quantity charts Chapter 7 embeds a structural-steel tonnage chart (component, MT and share of total) and side-by-side deck concrete / reinforcement panels.

6. Centralised styles.py Page geometry, palette, column types, caption spacing, table presets and the longtable builder live in one module. Chapter modules no longer call \setlength or write colour names by hand.

Adds tests/unit/test_report_styles.py covering all six items.

---

### Verification

| check | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| LaTeX errors on compile | 138 | **0** |
| tables with a repeating header | 2 | **50 / 50** |
| skipped rows (row-final `\\[6pt]`) | 418 | **0** |
| pages with body text in the footer band | — | **0** |
| Unit columns in Chapter 3 | 0 | **4** |
| UR / material chart includes | 0 / 0 | **1 / 2** |
| report length (20 m span, 3 girders, 5.9 m deck) | 53 pp | 57 pp |

Measured by recompiling both the original and the patched `.tex` with identical stubs (`tools/compare_reports.py`), plus a word-level PDF bounding-box scan for footer collisions.

`python -m pytest tests/unit -q` → **47 passed** (44 of them in `tests/unit/test_report_styles.py`), also verified on a fresh clone of this branch.

Branch is `report-layout-fixes` rather than `report/layout-and-style-fixes` because the repo already has a branch named `report`, which git rejects as a ref directory conflict.

Full write-up (files touched, `styles.py` structure, rationale, open polish) and the before/after PDFs are in the submitted technical-changes document.

body: # [Bug/UI] Project Location Displays as Unselected Even Though the Previous Location Is Retained and Used ### Description The Project Location field in Basic Inputs displays **"Select Location"**, suggesting that no location is selected. However, the application retains the previously selected location internally and uses it in the generated design report. This creates an inconsistency between the UI and the actual project state. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Open OsdagBridge and load a previously saved baseline `.osi` file containing a selected Project Location (Panjim, Goa). 2. Continue working with the loaded inputs and modify other parameters, such as span and carriageway width. 3. Observe that the Project Location field displays **"Select Location"**, even though the previously selected location is still being retained. 4. Generate the bridge design. 5. Generate the design report. 6. Check the Project Location field in Basic Inputs and the Project Location recorded in the generated report. ### Expected Behaviour The Basic Inputs UI should consistently display the active Project Location. If the previously selected location is retained and used for design, it should remain visible in the UI. If it has been cleared, the application should not silently continue using the previous location. ### Actual Behaviour - Basic Inputs displays **"Select Location"**. - The bridge design is generated using the retained project state. - The generated report displays **"Panjim, Goa"** as the Project Location. ### Evidence Attached screenshots:

title: [Bug] Material Take-off steel girder volume uses G1's area for every girder and disagrees with its own weight
body: ### Summary The steel girder volume in the Material Take-off is computed from girder G1's area alone and multiplied by the number of girders. The weight column sums each girder's own mass, so for unequal girders the volume and weight in the same table disagree. ### Description In `calculate_material_quantities` (`src/osdagbridge/core/boq/boq_generator.py`), the steel girder volume is `n_girders × (G1 area × span)`, while the weight sums each girder's own mass. **Works:** when all girders have identical sections, volume and weight agree. **Fails:** when girders differ (custom or unequal sections), the volume and weight in the same table contradict each other. Only the `.M1` member of each girder is read, so extra segments are ignored. ### Expected vs actual | | Expected | Actual | |---|---|---| | Steel girder total volume | Sum of each girder's area × span = 3.30 m³ | 2.70 m³ (3 × G1 area × span) | | Volume vs weight | Consistent (25.91 MT ÷ 7.85 = 3.30 m³) | Weight implies 3.301 m³, volume shows 2.70 m³ | ### Reproduction (no GUI, direct call) ```python from osdagbridge.core.boq import boq_generator as b A = "member_properties.girder_details.section_properties.area" M = "member_properties.girder_details.section_properties.mass" span, n = 30.0, 3 inp = {b.KEY_SPAN: span, b.KEY_TS_NO_OF_GIRDERS: n} areas = {1: 0.03, 2: 0.05, 3: 0.03} for g, a in areas.items(): inp[A + ".G%d.M1" % g] = a inp[M + ".G%d.M1" % g] = a * 7850.0 q = b.calculate_material_quantities(inp, {}) print("true total volume m3 :", round(span * sum(areas.values()), 3)) print("reported vol_total :", q["steel_girders_vol_total"]) print("reported wt_total MT :", q["steel_girders_wt_total"], "-> implied volume", round(float(q["steel_girders_wt_total"]) / 7.85, 3)) ``` Output: ``` true total volume m3 : 3.3 reported vol_total : 2.70 reported wt_total MT : 25.91 -> implied volume 3.301 ``` Screenshot: **Environment:** dev @ d74f56d (no upstream changes to `boq_generator.py` at time of testing), Windows, conda env `osdagbridge-env`. ### Root cause In `boq_generator.py`: ``` 142: girder_area = float(resolve_girder_value(inputs, "member_properties.girder_details.section_properties.area", 0)) 174: girder_vol = girder_area * span 181: mass_per_m = float(resolve_girder_value(inputs, "member_properties.girder_details.section_properties.mass", gi)) 183-184: except Exception: total_girder_mass += girder_area * span * 7850.0 186: girder_total_vol = n_girders * girder_vol ``` - Line 142 reads the area with index `0` (G1 only), and line 186 multiplies it by `n_girders`. - Line 181 reads the mass per girder (`gi`), so weight and volume diverge when girders differ. - The broad `except Exception` at lines 183-184 silently falls back to G1's area. - `resolve_girder_value` only resolves `.G{i+1}.M1`, so multi-segment girders are not handled. ### Suggested fix (not yet run in the repo) Replace lines 139-172 with the code below (adjust indentation), and delete the old mass loop at lines 179-184, because it would add the mass a second time. Line 186 can stay, since `girder_vol` becomes the per-girder average. ```python def _girder_area_m2(inputs, gi): area_key = "member_properties.girder_details.section_properties.area" try: a = float(resolve_girder_value(inputs, area_key, gi)) if a > 0: return a except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError): pass sec = "member_properties.girder_details.section_input." try: dw, tw, bft, tft, bfb, tfb = (float(resolve_girder_value(inputs, sec + k, gi)) for k in ( "web_depth", "web_thickness", "top_flange_width", "top_flange_thickness", "bottom_flange_width", "bottom_flange_thickness")) return (dw * tw + bft * tft + bfb * tfb) / 1e6 # mm -> m2 except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError): return 0.0 mass_key = "member_properties.girder_details.section_properties.mass" girder_total_vol, total_girder_mass = 0.0, 0.0 for gi in range(n_girders): a_i = _girder_area_m2(inputs, gi) girder_total_vol += a_i * span try: total_girder_mass += float(resolve_girder_value(inputs, mass_key, gi)) * span except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError): total_girder_mass += a_i * span * 7850.0 girder_vol = girder_total_vol / n_girders if n_girders else 0.0 # per-girder average for the formula row girder_area = girder_vol / span if span > 0 else 0.0 # keeps the existing formula line working ``` For multi-segment girders, multiply each segment's area by its length from the segment table (`KEY_MP_GD_SEGMENT_TABLE`). ### Related but distinct #84 (crash-barrier row of the same table, unit mismatch) and #102 (deck rebar and concrete rates in the same Material Take-off table). This issue covers the steel girder row.

title: [Bug] Material Take-off uses fixed 120 kg/m³ rebar and 2.5 t/m³ concrete for the deck, ignoring the designed reinforcement
body:
### Summary
The deck rebar and concrete weights in the Material Take-off are fixed multiples of the concrete volume (120 kg/m³ and 2.5 t/m³). They do not respond to the reinforcement the deck design computes.

### Description
`calculate_material_quantities` (`src/osdagbridge/core/boq/boq_generator.py`) computes the deck rebar weight as a constant 120 kg per m³ of concrete and the deck concrete weight as a constant 2.5 t/m³. It never reads the reinforcement computed by the deck design (bottom, top and distribution steel), and the concrete density is a literal constant in the code.

**Works:** deck concrete volume scales correctly with span, width and thickness.

**Fails:** rebar and concrete weights do not respond to the design. The same geometry with very different provided reinforcement gives identical weights. The report's deck design chapter (`chap5.py`) prints the designed reinforcement, but the take-off table does not reflect it.

### Expected vs actual
| | Expected | Actual |
|---|---|---|

title: # [Docs/CLI] README documents CLI usage but installed CLI entrypoint is a stub that ignores arguments
body:
**Environment**
- OsdagBridge `dev` @ `d74f56d` (2026-07-26)
- macOS (Intel), conda env `osdagbridge-env`, Python 3.12.16
- Finding type: **T6 (documentation/usage vs actual behavior)**

**Description**
`README.md` presents the project as supporting a CLI interface and documents example CLI commands, but the installed console script resolves to a stub implementation that prints a fixed message and ignores all arguments (including `--help`). This makes the documented CLI workflow unusable as written and can confuse users/contributors.

**README claims/examples**
- `README.md:4` — "It supports desktop (PySide6), web (Django + React), and CLI interfaces through a unified Python core."
- `README.md:18` — "The desktop GUI, web app, and CLI all reuse the same core for consistent behavior."
- `README.md:102` — documents `osdagbridge analyze project.yaml --solver native`
- `README.md:108` — documents `osdagbridge report project.yaml report.pdf`
- `README.md:154` — lists CLI code location: `src/osdagbridge/cli/`

**Actual behavior (evidence)**
- `pyproject.toml:85` declares console script: `osdagbridge-cli = "osdagbridge.cli.__main__:main"`
- `src/osdagbridge/cli/__main__.py`:
  ```py
  """CLI entrypoint."""
  def main():
      print("osdagbridge CLI (stub)")

  if __name__ == "__main__":
      main()
- Invocations print the stub and ignore arguments/flags (exit 0), e.g.:
- osdagbridge-cli --help → osdagbridge CLI (stub)
- osdagbridge-cli analyze project.yaml → osdagbridge CLI (stub)
(recorded in evidence/logs/phase1_entrypoints.txt; tests/test_phase1_packaging.py::test_cli_stub_ignores_args confirms stub behavior)
Expected behavior
Either (a) the CLI should implement (or clearly route to) the documented commands/flags, or (b) the README should clearly mark the CLI as unimplemented/stub and avoid presenting non-functional command examples as usable.
Actual behavior
README documents CLI support and example commands, but the CLI entrypoint is a stub that ignores arguments and provides no help/command handling.
Impact
- Users following README CLI examples cannot run analysis/report generation via the documented CLI.
- Misleading contributor/user expectations about available interfaces (desktop/web/CLI parity).
Suggested fix
- Implement argument parsing and the documented commands (analyze, report, etc.) in the CLI entrypoint, or
- Update README to clearly label the CLI as a stub/WIP, remove or annotate non-functional examples, and document the actual supported way to run/analyze (if any) until CLI is implemented.
- Consider aligning the documented executable name/usage (osdagbridge ... in README) with the installed console script name (osdagbridge-cli in pyproject.toml) if both are intended.
Duplicate check
Searched existing OsdagBridge issues (open+closed, full titles/bodies) for README/CLI/osdagbridge-cli/stub terms — no matching issue found (CLI-related UI "click" mentions in other issues are unrelated). (Not #96.)
Notes
src/osdagbridge/cli/commands.py exists in the source tree; this report is limited to the installed/documented entrypoint behavior observed at dev @ d74f56d.

title: # [Docs/Packaging] Inconsistent dependency declarations across `pyproject.toml`, `requirements.txt`, and `environment.yml`
body:
**Environment**
- OsdagBridge `dev` @ `d74f56d` (2026-07-26)
- Finding type: **T6 (documentation/packaging consistency)**

**Description**
The repository provides three dependency/install manifests (`pyproject.toml`, `requirements.txt`, `environment.yml`) that declare different package sets. This inconsistency makes installs and contributor setups ambiguous and increases the chance of broken or partially working environments (especially given that actual runtime requirements also differ; see related install issues).

**Observed declarations (as read from the repo)**

**`pyproject.toml` `[project].dependencies`**
```toml
scipy>=1.10.1
fiona
shapely
pydantic>=2.0
matplotlib>=3.5
openseespy>=3.2.2.6
opsvis>=1.0
xarray
requirements.txt
PySide6>=6.5.0,<=6.9.3
numpy>=1.21.0
scipy>=1.10.1
fiona
shapely
pydantic
xarray
ifcopenshell
openpyxl
environment.yml (summary)
- conda: osdag::osdag, matplotlib, fiona, shapely, scipy>=1.10.1, pydantic, xarray, python>=3.11,<3.13, pip
- pip: openseespy>=3.2.2.6, opsvis, -e .
Inconsistencies (examples)
- PySide6, numpy, ifcopenshell, openpyxl appear in requirements.txt but not in pyproject.toml deps.
- matplotlib, openseespy, opsvis appear in pyproject.toml/env but are missing from requirements.txt (and matplotlib not in requirements).
- osdag_core / PyYAML / navcube / OCC / plotly / pandas are used in source (see related finding) but are not consistently represented across manifests.
- environment.yml relies on osdag::osdag and -e . (with its own dep set), diverging from both requirements.txt and pyproject.toml.
Expected behavior
Install/dependency manifests should be consistent, clearly scoped (runtime vs dev/test vs optional extras vs conda), and aligned with the project’s actual requirements and documented install paths.
Actual behavior
Three manifests disagree on core/runtime packages, creating conflicting guidance for users and contributors.
Impact
- Users following different install instructions may get different, incomplete, or conflicting environments.
- Harder to reproduce bugs and to reason about which dependencies are truly required.
Suggested fix
- Establish a single source of truth for dependencies (e.g. pyproject.toml with optional extras) and generate/align requirements/conda environment from it where possible.
- Clearly document which manifest to use for which workflow (pip editable install, conda env, dev/test), and ensure each includes the packages needed for that workflow.
- Address the underlying missing/unused dependency issues (see related reports on pyproject.toml deps and osdag_core metadata).
Duplicate check
Searched existing OsdagBridge issues (open+closed, full titles/bodies) for requirements.txt / manifest-inconsistency packaging terms — no matching issue found (environment.yml appears only as environment context in unrelated issues). (Not #96.)

title: # [Bug/Install] `osdag_core` dependency metadata declares bogus `sqlite` package (breaks clean dependency resolution)
body:
**Environment**
- OsdagBridge `dev` @ `d74f56d` (2026-07-26), tested in conda env `osdagbridge-env` (Python 3.12.16)
- Observed in installed dependency: `osdag_core 0.0.0`
- Finding type: **T5 (installation/environment blocker)**

**Description**
The installed `osdag_core` package used with OsdagBridge declares `sqlite` as a runtime dependency in its package metadata. `sqlite` is not a valid/installable PyPI distribution for Python’s stdlib database module (the stdlib module is `sqlite3`), so this can break dependency resolution in clean environments.

**Steps to reproduce (environment/metadata check)**
1. In the OsdagBridge environment, inspect `osdag_core` metadata:
   ```python
   import importlib.metadata as m
   print(m.distribution("osdag_core").metadata.get_all("Requires-Dist"))
2. (Optional) pip index versions sqlite → no matching distribution.
Expected behavior
Dependency metadata should reference installable distributions only; stdlib sqlite3 should not be declared as a pip package dependency.
Actual behavior
osdag_core 0.0.0 Requires-Dist includes a bogus sqlite entry:
['pylatex', 'numpy', 'PyYaml', 'Click', 'pandas', 'sqlite', 'PySide6']
(evidence: evidence/logs/phase1_installed_meta.txt; tests/test_phase1_packaging.py::test_osdag_core_declares_bogus_sqlite_dep)
Impact
Can cause pip/resolver failures in fresh installs of the OsdagBridge stack (install-time blocker), depending on how dependencies are resolved.
Suggested fix
- If this is declared in osdag_core packaging: remove sqlite from Requires-Dist (stdlib sqlite3 needs no pip dependency), or replace with the correct external package only if a non-stdlib one is actually required.
- If the pin/source of osdag_core is controlled by OsdagBridge setup (environment.yml / install docs), ensure a corrected osdag_core build is referenced.
Duplicate check
Searched existing OsdagBridge issues (open+closed, full titles/bodies) for sqlite/osdag_core dependency-metadata terms — no matching packaging issue found (hits were unrelated DB/design issues such as #20/#42). (Not #96.)
Notes
Observed in the installed osdag_core dependency metadata in the test environment (not a source change in the OsdagBridge repo itself); reporting here as an OsdagBridge-ecosystem install blocker encountered during setup/testing.

title: # [Bug] Toggling input lock can crash when Additional Inputs dialog was never opened (`_additional_inputs_dialog` is None)
body:
**Environment**
- OsdagBridge `dev` @ `d74f56d` (2026-07-26)
- macOS (Intel), conda env `osdagbridge-env`, Python 3.12.16
- Finding type: **T3 (static, code-read; not executed as a runtime repro in this session)**

**Description**
Lock/unlock propagates state to the Additional Inputs dialog, but `InputDock.toggle_lock()` dereferences the dialog without checking whether it has been instantiated. `template_page` creates the dialog lazily, so toggling the input lock before ever opening Additional Inputs can raise `AttributeError` on `None`.

**Steps to reproduce (expected from code path)**
1. Launch OsdagBridge and open the plate girder module (do **not** open “Additional Inputs/Geometry”).
2. Trigger the input lock/unlock toggle (padlock / “Clear Results” → Continue path that flips lock state).

**Expected behavior**
Lock state changes safely regardless of whether the Additional Inputs dialog has been created.

**Actual behavior (from static analysis)**
`InputDock.toggle_lock()` calls `lock()` on `self.parent._additional_inputs_dialog` unconditionally; if the dialog was never created, this is `None`.

**Evidence (file:line, read-only)**
`src/osdagbridge/desktop/ui/docks/input_dock.py:856-859`:
```python
self.is_locked = not self.is_locked

# Update Additional Input State (Lock/Unlock)
self.parent._additional_inputs_dialog.lock(lock=self.is_locked)
src/osdagbridge/desktop/ui/template_page.py:124 initializes lazily:
self._additional_inputs_dialog: AdditionalInputs | None = None
Created on demand in _get_additional_inputs() (template_page.py:440-447), while other call sites guard with if self._additional_inputs_dialog is not None: (e.g. :454,615,862).
Suggested fix (diff sketch)
--- a/src/osdagbridge/desktop/ui/docks/input_dock.py
+++ b/src/osdagbridge/desktop/ui/docks/input_dock.py
@@
         self.is_locked = not self.is_locked

         # Update Additional Input State (Lock/Unlock)
-        self.parent._additional_inputs_dialog.lock(lock=self.is_locked)
+        dlg = getattr(self.parent, "_additional_inputs_dialog", None)
+        if dlg is not None:
+            dlg.lock(lock=self.is_locked)
Duplicate check
Searched existing issues (open+closed, full titles/bodies in notes/issues_raw.json) for _additional_inputs_dialog / related AttributeError-on-lock terms — no matching issue found. (Not #96.)
Notes
Static finding (code-read); a quick GUI confirm (toggle lock before opening Additional Inputs) would strengthen it.

title: [Bug] Loading a .osi file skips all custom-material validation — out-of-range material values load unchallenged
body:
### Summary
The `.osi` load path validates geometry and additional inputs, but **no
`material.*` key is ever validated**. A hand-edited `.osi` file can therefore
carry custom-material values far outside the limits the Material Properties
dialog enforces live (e.g. Fy 99999 MPa), and the file loads with
"Loaded OSI Successfully!".

### Reproduction
1. Open any saved `.osi` file in a text editor.
2. Add / edit: `material.girder.fy: 99999`, `material.girder.density: 5`,
   `material.deck.fck: -3` (all far outside the documented ranges
   Fy 100–1200 MPa, density 50–120 kN/m³, fck 10–80 MPa).
3. Load it in the app via **Load Input**.

**Expected:** "Invalid OSI File" rejection, same as an out-of-range span.

**Actual:** the file loads successfully; no error is shown.

### Minimal proof (headless, dev @ d74f56d)
`validate_osi_inputs({'material.girder.fy': 99999.0,
'material.girder.density': 5.0, 'material.deck.fck': -3.0})`
→ `is_valid = True`, `errors = []`

The exact same values *are* rejected by `BridgeInputValidator.validate_material_inputs`:
- fy 99999 → corrected to 1200.0
- density 5 → corrected to 50.0
- fck -3 → corrected to 10.0

### Root cause
`osdagbridge/core/utils/osi_validator.py`:
- `_BASIC_KEYS` (lines 82–86) contains only span / carriageway / skew.
- `_ADDITIONAL_KEYS` (lines 89–111) contains many numeric limits but **no
  `material.*` keys**.
- `validate()` (lines 142–157) iterates only these two lists and calls
  `validate_basic_inputs` / `validate_additional_inputs`, so
  `validate_material_inputs` — the check the live Material Properties dialog
  uses (`_on_material_field_edited`) — is **unreachable from the load path**
  (`template_page.py loadOSI_inputs`, line 847).

The module's own docstring states the goal: *"keeps the load-time rules in
lock-step with the interactive rules"* — for materials this lock-step is
currently missing.

### Suggested fix
Add the material keys to the OSI validation loop, e.g.:

```diff
--- a/src/osdagbridge/core/utils/osi_validator.py
+++ b/src/osdagbridge/core/utils/osi_validator.py
@@ _ADDITIONAL_KEYS = [
+    # custom material limits — same rules the Material dialog enforces live
+    KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_DENSITY, KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_FY, KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_FU,
+    KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_E, KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_G, KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_POISSON,
+    KEY_MATERIAL_GIRDER_THERMAL,
+    KEY_MATERIAL_DECK_DENSITY, KEY_MATERIAL_DECK_FCK, KEY_MATERIAL_DECK_FCTM,
+    KEY_MATERIAL_DECK_ECM, KEY_MATERIAL_DECK_THERMAL,
     KEY_TS_GIRDER_SPACING, ...
 ]
```
and in validate(), route these keys through
self._bridge_validator.validate_material_inputs (they currently return
None from validate_additional_inputs, which doesn't know them).
Impact
Hand-edited or third-party-generated .osi files bypass every custom-material
limit; garbage values then flow into analysis and the design report (the app's
own Save/Load round trip is unaffected, which is why this only shows with
edited files).

title: clarification required-Stress Limitation displays 0.9 × Fy instead of the stated Fy / γM0
body:
Summary:

The Girder Design → Design Check → Stress Limitation card consistently displays a limiting stress equal to 90% of the selected steel yield strength.

However, the formula displayed in the application is:

σ ≤ Fy / γM0

Steps to Reproduce:

2. Open Girder Design → Design Check → Stress Limitation.

For E350A: 350 / 1.10 = 318.18 MPa.

For custom steel: 520 / 1.10 = 472.73 MPa.

The displayed values do not match these calculations.

Clarification Required:

Is the 0.9 reduction intentional under the applicable design provision? If yes, should the displayed formula or its explanation be updated to reflect the actual calculation?
